Exceptional start-up founders take the "yellow circle" to open up about their personal struggles and challenges, so that these stories may be a source of learning, encouragement, and inspiration for other entrepreneurs.

title: Cross-Border Wholesale Connectivity: Building a More Connected Financial System
speakers: Dr. Alexandra Hachmeister; Tom Mutton; Miguel Díaz; Peerapong Thonnagith; Ivan Odonnat; Alan Lim
description:
As digital money, tokenized assets and next-generation financial infrastructures gain traction around the world, jurisdictions and institutions are adopting a growing range of technologies, infrastructure models and settlement systems. While this diversity is driving innovation, it also raises an important question: how can increasingly interconnected financial systems continue to operate seamlessly across borders — without waiting for a single global standard to emerge first?

This panel brings together the institutions alongside policymakers and innovators from Asia, Europe and the UK to discuss what regional cooperation actually requires in practice: unified ledgers, synchronisation mechanisms, privacy-preserving technologies, and the governance arrangements that let independently built systems trust one another.

The discussion will examine the technical, legal, operational and regulatory challenges involved in scaling these regional models, and explore how deeper connectivity between them — rather than a single unified global system — may be the more realistic path to an interconnected financial system.

title: Is Cross-Border Mutual Recognition Through Sandboxes Now Closer or Further?
speakers: Friederike Lange; Shweta Rajpal Kohli; Owureku Asare; Juan Pablo Ortega; Arjun Vir Singh
description: Expanding across fragmented regional markets forces digital finance startups into repetitive licensing cycles that multiply compliance costs and stall international scale. Recent agreements between Rwanda’s central bank and its counterparts in Ghana and Kenya to establish fintech licence passporting show that cross-border supervisory reciprocity is moving from principle to practice. A recent survey by TechCabal Research revealed that 62.5% of regional fintechs already operate internationally or plan to, with an identical proportion backing passporting frameworks. This session convenes financial regulators and founders to examine how central banks can align supervisory frameworks and establish mutual recognition standards without compromising financial stability or compliance oversight.

title: The Speed-Trust Paradox: Can Trust Keep Up with Agentic Finance? - Powered by MongoDB
description: As AI in finance shifts from advising to acting, institutions face a speed–trust paradox. Using MAS' Safeguards for Agentic Finance at Runtime (SAFR) framework as a lens, this discussion explores why the data moat must evolve from volume to an operational foundation that carries trusted identity, mandate, disposition and audit data across agents, workflows and jurisdictions.
description_zh: 隨著金融領域的 AI 從提供建議轉向採取行動，機構面臨速度與信任之間的矛盾。本場討論以新加坡金融管理局（MAS）的代理型金融執行期間保障（Safeguards for Agentic Finance at Runtime，SAFR）架構為視角，探討為何資料護城河必須從資料量優勢，演進為一套營運基礎，讓可信的身分、授權、處置及稽核資料得以跨代理、工作流程及司法管轄區流通。

title: Owning Your AI, Advancing Agentic Banking - Powered by Huawei
description: What separates leading banks is not how many models or agents they deploy, but whether they can safely scale their own intelligence in core production at controlled cost. Models will keep changing; banks must stay in charge of how that intelligence is built, operated and evolved. This session unpacks the architecture behind it: open architecture and open source for freedom to choose; full-lifecycle Token management for controllable cost; knowledge and engineering assets for faster reuse; and an Agent marketplace with Skills for business-led assembly.

title: [Booth 2G25] Trust in regulated industries
description: How regulated businesses can deliver great AI-powered customer experiences while staying safe, secure, and compliant.

title: VMware Migration and Multi Cloud Management - Powered by Beyondsoft
description: Explore how Beyondsoft helps enterprises navigate VMware migration challenges and simplify multi-cloud operations. Through a real-world migration case, discover practical strategies to minimize downtime and migration risks. See how Beyondsoft’s Cloud Management Platform (CMP) enables unified management, monitoring, and cost optimization across cloud environments.

title: Global Metacase and Economic World Model Challenges - Powered by GIFTS@NTU
description: Can AI effectively simulate markets and social systems and its agents out-reason human experts in specialized tasks? Two new global competitions aim to find out. Economic World Model Challenge tests how well participants can create digital twins for city planning, (onchain) financial markets, etc., on powerful platforms such as HoloBit, while Metacase challenge tests agents' ability to conduct complex analyses and draw sound inferences from business and business cases. Join this session for live demos, learn why economic world models and metacases matter for risk, policy and investment, and find out how your team can partake in an international community pushing the frontier of AI for business and social science.

title: The Price of Intelligence: AI's Expanding Possibilities - Powered by Nucleus Software
description: AI is becoming more accessible, opening new possibilities for innovation in financial services. This session explores those possibilities through the economics of building and running AI, regulatory responsibilities and environmental sustainability. It considers whether commoditisation could reduce the cost of wider adoption or shift where those costs sit. The aim is to offer a balanced perspective on AI's promise and the considerations that shape its long-term value.

title: What Quantum Computing could Change in Finance, and What Banks can Build Today
description:
Banks are already preparing for quantum computers capable of threatening today’s cryptography. What could machines of that capability enable in finance, and what useful applications might emerge earlier as hardware evolves?

Carlos Kuchkovsky, CEO and co-founder of QCentroid, will examine these questions across investment, risk, treasury and payments, connecting computational capabilities with potential improvements in solution quality, speed and scale. Using the QuantumOps framework, he will show how banks can prioritise opportunities, develop applications and benchmark classical, hybrid and quantum approaches against strong classical baselines and financial requirements, including comparisons between quantum configurations.

The session follows the application lifecycle into existing financial workflows, showing how teams can use an approved version while separately calibrating and benchmarking candidate improvements as algorithms, hardware and business needs evolve. Attendees will leave with practical criteria for choosing what to build today, assessing whether a new approach adds value and deciding when an application is ready for operational use.

title: Scaling Real-Time Payments: Adoption, Commercial Innovation and the Economics of Inclusion
speakers: Dr. Veerathai Santiprabhob; Kosta Peric; Jean Bosco Iyacu; Sara Brites; Sateesh Palagiri; Pat Patel
description:
Instant payments can reach millions of the unbanked but only if the economics work for everyone building the rails. Around the world, national real-time payment systems are proving that speed and inclusion can coexist, yet many struggle to balance universal access with commercial viability. Getting that balance right is now a defining test of payments strategy.

You will learn: how to design instant payment schemes that serve the underserved without eroding sustainability; which governance and pricing models drive long-term adoption; and what lessons successful national roadmaps offer to markets still building theirs. Miss this session, and you risk designing a system that scales in usage but never in value.

title: What Will Tokenised Markets Settle In?
speakers: Toh Wee Kee; Scott Lucas; Gildas Le Treut; Michael Casey
description:
Every tokenised asset needs tokenised money to settle against, but what form will it be? Tokenisation promises to change how bonds, funds, private markets and real-world assets are issued, traded and settled. Yet without a trusted, programmable cash leg, it remains stuck at the pilot stage. Global banks are bringing deposits on-chain, and stablecoins have already reached some scale as internet-native dollars. Both are looking to be part of the settlement layer of the next financial system.

This session brings together leaders who will discuss which form of money corporates and institutions will trust for atomic settlement, collateral and liquidity, whether bank money and internet-native money will compete or interoperate, and what must be in place for tokenised markets to scale.

title: Payments Went Global. Can the Tech Keep Up?
speakers: Yogesh Sangle; Ashish Mangal; Violas Xiao; Nilixa Devlukia
description: Payments move across borders in seconds. Building the technology to support them is a different challenge: connecting to local payment rails, adapting to market requirements, and scaling reliable products across regions. This panel looks at the infrastructure and product choices that help payment companies expand across the US, Europe, the Gulf and Asia—and where local licensing still shapes the roadmap. Founders leave with practical ideas for sequencing market entry, reducing integration friction and building payment systems that can scale globally.

title: Driving Financial Inclusion and Shared Prosperity in an Age of Uncertainty
speakers: William Ury; Alexandre Chade; Yang Peng; Luay Obaidi; Carrie Suen
description:
From the ancient markets of Mesopotamia to today’s digital corridors linking Iraq, Brazil and Asia, trade has always been about more than goods. It is how people build livelihoods, trust and opportunity. Today, geopolitical uncertainty, regionalisation and fast advances in AI are redrawing the paths to prosperity. Yet what entrepreneurs and families want remains strikingly similar across borders.

William Ury, co-founder of the Harvard Program on Negotiation and author of Possible, argues that progress comes from listening deeply and finding shared interests, even in a divided world. This session puts that idea to work in finance. Alexandre Chade brings Brazil’s experience through Dotz, Luay Obaidi shows how Qi Card is widening access to digital payments in Iraq, and Yang Peng sets out how Ant International connects consumers, merchants and small businesses across markets. The panel asks not only what technology can do, but whom it serves. Payments, AI and connectivity are the means; dignity, opportunity and shared prosperity are the purpose.

The discussion also tackles a central tension. Global trade keeps finding ways to grow, yet smaller enterprises and underserved households still face fragmented rules, limited access and uneven digital capabilities. What can private-sector ingenuity achieve on its own, and where must governments and institutions build the conditions for inclusive growth?

title: AI, Fintech and the Rise of India's Next Innovation Hubs: From Eastern India to the World
speakers: Sujeet Kumar; Abhay Kumar Singh; Preeti Dawra
description: India's technology and financial landscape is expanding beyond its traditional centres, creating new opportunities for states to shape the country's economic future. Bihar's ambition to become an AI hub and Odisha's emergence as a fintech hub reflect two distinct approaches to technology-led transformation. How can these states build globally competitive innovation ecosystems, develop talent, foster entrepreneurship and attract international partnerships? The discussion explores how state-level innovation can strengthen India's national competitiveness while connecting emerging technology hubs with global markets, investment and opportunities.

title: Quantum Security Questionnaire Results Sharing by MAS
description: Hear from MAS on their findings from their recent Quantum Security Questionnaire with Financial Institutions.

title: Beyond the QR Code: What Moves China's Money Next? [Conducted in Mandarin]
speakers: Guo Lin; Chen Yu; Cynthia Ding
description: China built the world's most pervasive mobile payments system on a black-and-white square. But when nearly every transaction runs through a QR code, where does the next leap come from? With the e-CNY pushing into wallets and cross-border rails like mBridge testing new models for settling value between central banks, the architecture of Chinese money is being redrawn. The panel unpacks which layers (digital currency, embedded finance, AI-driven credit or cross-border settlement) will capture the next wave of value. It also looks at what interoperability means for incumbents and foreign players, and how China's choices could set the template for payments across Asia.
description_zh: 中國憑藉一個黑白方格，建立了全球最普及的行動支付系統。但當幾乎每筆交易都透過 QR 碼完成，下一次躍進將從何而來？隨著數位人民幣（e-CNY）進入錢包，以及 mBridge 等跨境軌道試驗中央銀行之間價值結算的新模式，中國的貨幣架構正被重新描繪。本場座談將解析哪些層面，包括數位貨幣、嵌入式金融、AI 驅動的信貸或跨境結算，將掌握下一波價值。也將探討互通性對既有業者與外國參與者的意義，以及中國的選擇如何可能成為亞洲各地支付發展的範本。

title: Banking the Next Billion: Enabling Secure and Inclusive Growth in an Agentic AI Economy
speakers: Rama Mohan Rao Amara; Ailish Campbell; Masashi Namatame; Aparna Jhajharia
description:
As AI becomes increasingly agentic, able to act, transact and make decisions on behalf of individuals and businesses, the opportunity to expand financial inclusion and economic participation has never been greater. But with that potential comes new risk. This session explores how governments, financial institutions and technology providers can work together to build trusted digital ecosystems that are secure, interoperable and inclusive by design. From managing fraud and strengthening cyber resilience to advancing digital identity, cross-border connectivity and user education across every part of society, panellists will discuss how to ensure the benefits of AI-driven financial services reach more people and small businesses without creating new barriers to access.

Central Question: How do we make sure AI agents that act on people's behalf widen access to finance, rather than create new risks and new barriers?

title: Banking 5.0: The Rise of the Agentic Bank
description: Smart economies are beginning to make decisions and act across transport, energy, commerce and finance. Banking’s next shift may follow: AI agents could move from advising customers to initiating transactions, coordinating services and managing financial outcomes on their behalf. That prospect raises a structural question: can systems built around human instructions, batch payments and familiar forms of accountability support finance conducted at machine speed? The answer depends on more than a smarter interface. It requires new architecture, agentic compliance and risk controls that preserve human oversight where it matters. Banking 5.0 sets out the case for that transition and what separates structural change from a chatbot layered over legacy systems.
description_zh: 智慧經濟體正開始在交通、能源、商業與金融領域做出決策並採取行動。銀行業的下一波轉變可能隨之而來：AI 代理可能從向客戶提供建議，進一步代客戶發起交易、協調服務並管理財務成果。這種前景引出了一個結構性問題：以人類指令、批次支付及熟悉的問責形式為基礎的系統，能否支援以機器速度運行的金融活動？答案不僅取決於更智慧的介面，還需要新的架構、代理型法遵機制，以及能在關鍵之處保留人類監督的風險控制。「Banking 5.0」將闡述這項轉型的理由，以及真正的結構性變革與在舊有系統上疊加聊天機器人之間的差別。

title: Digital Bank-Agentic AI in SME Finance - Powered by WeBank
location: Global SME Finance Forum Experience Centre (Hall 5)
description:
This workshop is a working session on AI practice among the world's top digital banks. It is built on decisions that banks have already handed to AI, not on product roadshows. Across the SME finance journey — credit, pricing, tenor, servicing — participants will hear what the AI actually looked at, what it decided, which step still had to stay with a human, and what went wrong. The question behind the session is simple: where has AI moved from speeding up the process to making the business decision itself, and what does it take to get there. Participants will leave with a map they can act on: which decisions AI is already making in SME finance today, how the leading digital banks are funding and organising that work, and where the line between machine and human should sit. WeBank, China's first digital bank, will host the session and open with our own AI practice — what we have put into production, what we have deliberately kept out of its hands, and what we would do differently.

title: In Conversation with Dan Katz, First Deputy Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund
description:
What happens to the economy when AI can act on our behalf?

AI agents already write code and handle many customer queries, and they are beginning to make purchases and payments. As they become more capable, they could change how businesses operate, how work is organized and how money moves, opening the way to new products, services, and sources of growth.

The spread of agentic AI also raises hard questions, especially about jobs. Which roles will change, what new kinds of work will emerge, and how can people build the skills to work alongside AI? In this fireside chat, IMF First Deputy Managing Director Dan Katz will discuss the economic promise of agentic AI, the concerns that come with it, and what policymakers can do to help workers and economies adapt.

description: Fireside chat: Connecting financial ecosystems: Luxembourg and Singapore on the future of payments and digital finance - Speakers: Chek-Tchung Foo, Project Director - Singapore Payments Network at The Association of Banks in Singapore and Ananda Kautz, Member of the Management Board at The Luxembourg Bankers' Association (ABBL)

title: [Booth 2E13] SWDA: AI Skills @ Work Series
description:
AI is changing the way we work but are organisations and their people ready?

Join Skills & Workforce Development Agency (SWDA) for a practical conversation on building an AI-ready workforce. Together with leaders from UOB, Singtel, Secured Vision, the panel will discuss how AI is reshaping everyday tasks, the skills employees will need, and the role organisations play in enabling meaningful adoption.

From closing capability gaps to learning through real work, the session will provide practical perspectives on empowering employees to use AI responsibly, enhance decision-making, and translate new capabilities into tangible business outcomes.

title: The Autonomous Economy: Where the Intelligence Layer Meets Programmable Finance
speakers: Akio Isowa; Douglas Feagin; Stephen Karpin; Anthony Thomas
description: Imagine an economy where software doesn't just recommend decisions—it makes them, negotiates them, and settles them, all without a human in the loop. That future arrives when agentic AI meets programmable money. Autonomous agents that can transact, and digital money that can execute logic on its own, together unlock machine-speed commerce that today's financial rails were never built to handle. Learn how agentic AI and programmable money combine to reshape payments, settlement, and value exchange, what new risks emerge when agents transact autonomously, and how institutions should prepare for an economy that runs itself.

title: Next Gen Leaders AMA: Who Builds What Comes Next? Rewiring Talent for AI and Quantum Finance
description:
AI and quantum are moving faster than the workforce built to run them. In this Ask-Me-Anything, Next Gen Leader Lisa Schroeder, Managing Director, QAI Ventures interviews Clyde Seepersad, Senior Vice President & General Manager, Education, Linux Foundation on how skills, credentials and open collaboration are reshaping who gets to build the next financial system. The last ten minutes are open to the floor, so bring your questions.

About the Next Gen Leaders initiative:

The Next Gen Leaders initiative recognises and supports the rising generation of leaders shaping the future of finance and technology. The initiative aims to identify aspiring entrepreneurs, innovators, builders, and early-career professionals, anchor them to the GFTN community, empower them with fintech knowledge, leadership skills, and entrepreneurial access, and connect them globally through GFTN’s ecosystem.

title: From Intelligence to Action: The New Architecture of Competitive Advantage
speakers: Richard Pu; Richard Wormald; Leong Yung Chee; Magnus Haglind; Ronit Ghose
description: AI is moving beyond generating insights and assisting decisions to taking action — planning, coordinating and executing increasingly complex workflows. This shift towards agentic AI has implications far beyond technology, challenging the operating models, organisational structures and assumptions through which businesses have traditionally competed. As intelligence becomes more accessible, competitive advantage may depend less on who has the best AI and more on who can redesign their organisation, infrastructure and decision-making to turn intelligence into outcomes at scale. This session explores how agentic AI is reshaping the architecture of business from the systems that connect people, data and machines to the operating models that enable speed, adaptability and differentiation. In a world where AI can act, what will separate the leaders from the laggards and where will tomorrow’s competitive advantage really reside?

title: Ghost in the machine: Building Chocolate Finance's software engineering agents on Bedrock AgentCore
description: Chocolate Finance will discuss their AI journey across the organisation, focusing on the improvements made in the software engineering team. Listen to how they built a family of engineering agents on AWS Bedrock AgentCore, ensuring compliant, scalable and extensible AI-driven engineering.

title: Agentic Banking Roadmap - From Workflow to Governed Digital Workforce - Powered by Shenzhen Farben Information Technology Co., Ltd
description:
Agent Provisioning starts by unfolding a manageable workflow, to find where time and cost concentrate. Each step is scored for agent fit, then marked Replace, Assist, or Hold. Regulated decisions default to human-assisted.

Agent Solution Design turns findings into a supervisor-and-specialist agent architecture. Every agent is specified like a role, with an allow-listed toolset, grounded memory, and built-in guardrails and a kill switch. A thin-slice prototype is dual-run against the human baseline.

Agent Engineering promotes proven agents through UAT, Pre-Production drills then Production, and a staged rollout: dark run, canary, assist mode, then replace mode.

Agentic Governance runs an Agent OS, the “HR system” for digital employees (Agents). A registry, a runtime hook gateway, and continuous testing track accuracy, efficiency, consistency, and token economics.

Agents that fail are replaced

This session explores the “AI Dividend”, showing how practical first steps can compound into greater productivity and stronger business outcomes. Through Singapore SME examples, audience interaction and live demonstrations, discover how businesses and workers can move from uncertainty to action, creating shared benefits for employees, customers and the wider community.

title: [Booth 6C21] Higher Approvals, Lower Fraud: How Networks, Risk Platforms and Orchestrators Win Together
description: Every payment comes down to two goals: higher payment success rates and lower fraud losses. As payment methods evolve, fraud tactics evolve with them, and merchants are caught between approving more transactions and stopping more fraud. This panel brings together Mastercard, TrustDecision and Yuno, representing the card network, the risk platform and the payment orchestrator. In three rounds, speakers will first look at how payment methods and fraud tactics are changing, and how merchants can lift payment success rates. They will then cover the solutions: Mastercard's Identity Insights for Transactions and Ethoca Alerts, both integrated by TrustDecision, and TrustDecision's end-to-end risk monitoring from registration and login to marketing and payment. Finally, they will share real orchestration success stories and risk monitoring results.

Drawing on experiences from banks, fintechs and technology providers active in Italy, the discussion will examine practical applications of Generative and Agentic AI, how to identify high-impact use cases, establish effective governance frameworks and measure business outcomes beyond technical performance.

title: Owning Your Intelligence: From AI Adoption to AI at Scale
description: The first wave of AI was about proving what intelligence can do. The next challenge is putting it to work at scale. For financial institutions, AI must operate across fragmented systems, distributed operations, regulatory boundaries, and decades of technology investments. Success is no longer determined by models alone, but by the ability to operationalise intelligence while maintaining Scalability, Sustainability and Security. This keynote explores how leading financial institutions are moving beyond AI experimentation by building the engineering capabilities, operating foundations, and integration frameworks required to deploy intelligence across existing systems, processes, governance structures, and talent. The goal is not to rebuild the enterprise, but to unlock the value of AI at scale.

title: First Steps into FinTech – Four Learning Journeys from Odisha
description:
Starting a career in FinTech is harder than it looks from inside the industry. The skills employers ask for move quickly, entry-level roles are narrowing, and a graduate can hold a strong degree and still not know what the first step is.

Odisha is investing in FinTech and in the Global Capability Centres that follow it. That makes the question a practical one for the state's graduates: how do you build the specific capabilities those employers hire for, and how do you get close enough to the industry to be seen by one?

The Certificate in FinTech and InsurTech was built to answer it. Over five months, participants move through online modules, a two-week SDI bootcamp in Bhubaneswar, and a capstone project set by industry. They are mentored through the work, assessed by practitioners rather than graded on paper, and recognised publicly at the end of it. Those who complete the programme stay connected to the sector afterwards through the GFTN Knowledge Circle and GFTN's placement efforts.

Four of them take the stage here: two Global Pathfinders and two MUFG Young Innovators. We’ll walk through the programme as they lived it, from the skills they brought in, to what the capstone asked of them that they had not expected, to how they have grown as professionals since.

title: One World, Many Rails: Defining the Next Chapter of Money Movement
speakers: Brad Garlinghouse; Richard Teng; Umar Farooq; Meagen Burnett; Ralph Hamers; Pradyumna Agrawal
description: Money moves globally, but the rails beneath it don't speak the same language. Instant payment systems, stablecoins, card networks, correspondent banking, and CBDCs are all racing to define how value crosses borders—and no single winner is emerging. The future isn't one universal rail; it's many, and the real challenge is making them interoperate without friction, fragmentation, or lost trust. Learn how the competing rails of global money movement are converging and colliding, what interoperability actually requires across systems and jurisdictions, and where the next chapter of cross-border payments is really being written.
description_zh: 資金在全球流動，但其底層軌道卻使用不同的語言。即時支付系統、穩定幣、卡組織網絡、通匯銀行業務與央行數位貨幣（CBDC），都在競相定義價值如何跨境流動，但沒有任何一方成為唯一贏家。未來不會只有一條通用軌道，而是多條並存；真正的挑戰是讓它們能夠互通，避免摩擦、碎片化與信任流失。本場將說明全球資金流動中相互競爭的軌道如何融合與碰撞、跨系統及司法管轄區的互通性究竟需要什麼，以及跨境支付的下一篇章實際正在哪裡譜寫。

title: Built to Exit: How Cap Tables Make or Break the Endgame
speakers: Kshitij Golwalkar; Jonathan Whittle; Adrian Li; Yuan Lee Chung; Natasha Hartoro
description:
Every founder dreams of the exit. Far fewer plan for it.

In a funding cycle shaped by lofty valuations and layered rounds, many promising companies find their path to exit blocked by the very capital that fueled their growth. Complex cap tables, preference stacks, and misaligned shareholders can turn a willing acquirer into a walk-away, or a good outcome into a stalemate.

This session, co-hosted with Singapore Venture Capital Association, brings together investors for a candid conversation about what really stands between a startup and its exit. We’ll examine how high valuations and shareholder misalignment create friction when it matters most, and ask a harder question: how can founders and investors recognize early when to pivot or call time, before too much capital makes either option painful?

Expect frank views, real lessons, and practical takeaways for anyone raising or backing startups today.

title: Technology, Capital and Geoeconomics: The Asia-Middle East Corridor
speakers: Abdulrahman Hesham Al Sowaidi; Jawed Ashraf; Assoc. Prof. Dr. Nguyen Huu Huan; Sopnendu Mohanty
description: Technology and capital are no longer neutral conduits of commerce; they are instruments and pressure points in geoeconomic competition. Yet fragmentation has not ended integration. It has made its terms more contested. The Asia–Middle East corridor crystallises the challenge: how to deepen financial and digital connectivity while managing exposure to strategic chokepoints, incompatible systems and concentrated dependencies. Its test is whether interoperable infrastructure and practical cooperation can turn interdependence into resilience and give shape to a more trusted architecture of finance.

Can the company turn its reach across PayPal, Venmo and Braintree into a broader role in people’s financial lives? At SFF2026, CEO Enrique Lores joins a candid conversation about the choices, trade-offs and execution required to move beyond payments, and how much reinvention a quarter-century-old fintech can really pull off.

title: The Future of Banking: Beyond Payments
description:
The way money moves is entering a new era, driven by real-time payments, digitalization, and tokenization. This transformation is reshaping not only payments, but also the role of banks and the broader financial ecosystem.

The session will explore how banking needs to evolve and what the future of finance could look like in this new era.

title: The Agentic Enterprise: Accountability and Containment When the Machine Decides
speakers: Richard Tong; Lukasz Kubicki; Casey Klyszeiko; Alan Lim; Irene Liu
description:
Agentic AI has moved from pilots to systems that touch real credit decisions, real client money and real compliance rules, and the institutions getting the governance right this year are setting the ceiling for the next decade. This session examines where accountability sits once an agent, not a person, initiates the action, across risk, audit and reporting lines — and then confronts the scenario most institutions would rather not discuss: what actually happens in the moments after an agent goes wrong.

An agent doesn't take a coffee break. When it fails, it can fail at machine speed, across every transaction it touches, before a human even notices. So the real test isn't whether agents fail, but how fast an institution can contain them when they do, and who is authorised to make that call. This discussion moves from the accountability question to the operational one: what real-time containment looks like in practice, where autonomous systems are most likely to break, and how to build the kill switches and safeguards that limit the blast radius before autonomy is extended any further.

Attendees leave with a sharper view of the controls that need to exist before autonomy is extended further. One of the key questions the panel will look to dive deeper into: Who is accountable when an autonomous agent makes a bad call, moves client money, or silently breaks a compliance rule?
description_zh: 代理型 AI 已從試點走向涉及真實信貸決策、真實客戶資金與實際法遵規則的系統，而今年能做好治理的機構，正為未來十年奠定發展上限。本場將檢視，一旦發起行動的是代理而非人，在風險、稽核與匯報體系中，責任應歸於何處；接著直面多數機構寧可不談的情境：代理出錯後的最初幾個瞬間，究竟會發生什麼？代理不會休息喝咖啡。當它失效時，可能在人類察覺之前，就以機器速度在所接觸的每筆交易中接連出錯。因此，真正的考驗不在於代理是否會失效，而在於機構能多快控制失效的代理，以及誰獲授權做出這個決定。本場討論將從問責問題轉向營運問題：即時遏制在實務中是什麼樣貌、自主系統最可能在哪些地方出問題，以及如何在進一步擴大自主權之前，建立緊急停用機制與防護措施，以限制影響範圍。與會者將更清楚了解，在進一步擴大自主權之前，必須具備哪些控制措施。本場座談將深入探討的一個關鍵問題是：當自主代理做出錯誤判斷、移動客戶資金，或悄悄違反法遵規則時，誰應負責？

title: Designing for Real Life: Innovating for Financial Health
speakers: Moritz Gastl; Princess Charm Balingit; Shailesh Baidwan; David Symington; Bernadette Romulo Puyat
description:
Improving financial health takes more than better products. It requires regulators, financial institutions, fintechs, and policymakers to rethink how financial services are designed, delivered, and understood, particularly in emerging markets where income patterns, consumer behaviours, and financial needs can vary widely.

As a continuation from the ASEAN Financial Health Challenge, this panel brings together leaders across policy, fintech, banking, and insurance to examine how public-private collaboration can turn innovation into better financial outcomes. The discussion dives into how technology and human-centred design can address deep financial health challenges, where education needs to complement innovation, and how fintechs are developing and scaling new approaches across ASEAN.

The panel will conclude with an unveiling and the prize presentation of the 3 winners of the ASEAN Financial Health Challenge.

title: One Network, Millions of Bills, Billions of Lives: The Infrastructure Behind Interoperable Bill Payments - Powered by NPCI
description: Bharat Connect is an interoperable bill payment system, the only platform across the globe to enable millions of customers for paying their utility bills. This session will cover the impact of the infrastructure and the effect it has on utility service providers.
description_zh: Bharat Connect 是一套可互通的帳單支付系統，也是全球唯一能讓數百萬名客戶繳付公用事業帳單的平台。本場將介紹這項基礎設施所帶來的影響，以及它對公用事業服務提供者的作用。

title: When the Value of a Enterprise Can Be Seen, Understood and Trusted - Powered by ValueMap Global
description:
How can financial institutions assess a growing business when revenue, receivables and cash flow tell different stories?

Through an illustrative corporate financing case, Adam Lin, Founder and CEO of ValueMap Global, will examine how AI can help analyse company information, connect findings to financial and transaction evidence, and identify opportunities and questions requiring further review. The session will also explore how assessments should change when new information arrives.

Drawing on experience in financial services, Adam will introduce Enterprise Value Intelligence and its potential applications in business lending, leasing and receivables finance. He will discuss the roles of AI and analysts, alongside workspace and API integration options.

Attendees will gain a framework for evaluating AI-assisted due diligence through factual accuracy, evidence coverage, analyst rework and total review time, helping them assess whether AI outputs can support their teams’ everyday work.

Sending assets across borders, receiving payments, or making everyday transfers should feel simple and effortless, with the trust and confidence that comes from knowing your assets remain yours and under your control. Imagine a more connected way to move, spend, and grow your digital assets, all through one seamless experience, powered by stablecoins and built around trust. Join us to explore this vision for the future and experience it come to life.

description: Digital-first doesn’t mean physical cards are disappearing. For Reap, they remain a critical bridge between digital financial services and everyday spending. In this fireside chat, discover how the fintech approached its expansion into Latin America, where launching physical card programmes meant navigating new production, personalization and delivery requirements. Reap shares how, with Thales D1, it built a repeatable issuance model designed to reduce the complexity of entering new markets, accelerate programme launches and provide greater visibility across the card journey. A practical discussion on what it really takes to scale physical card issuance at the speed of digital.

description:

title: Pay It Forward
description: Whether you're a student starting out, a finance professional planning a career pivot, or a startup founder facing a specific business challenge, Pay It Forward connects you with established industry professionals for face-to-face, one-to-one mentorship. It's a chance to get advice from people who have already worked through the challenges you're facing. Sessions are 15 minutes long and take place at the Pay It Forward Lounge in Hall 3, from 18 to 20 November, 1:10pm to 4.30pm. Come with one specific question or challenge, and leave with focused, practical advice.

title: Money is Programmable. Can Tokenized Markets Follow?
speakers: Carolyn Weinberg; Dr. Tara Rice; Stephen Richardson; Gracie Lin; Emma Joyce
description: For decades, financial innovation meant new products on old rails. That lens no longer explains where control is concentrating. Money 1.0 digitised value. Money 2.0 networked it. Money 3.0 makes it programmable — value that carries its own logic, constraints and compliance, settling toward atomic, with AI agents as first-class transactors. But is this a structural shift, or digitisation in new clothes? This opening session looks to separate architecture from hype and asks the question that matters: How far can programmable money along with tokenized financial products go?
description_zh: 數十年來，金融創新意味著在舊軌道上推出新產品。這種視角已無法解釋控制權正在向何處集中。Money 1.0 將價值數位化；Money 2.0 將其網絡化；Money 3.0 則使其可程式化，讓價值自帶邏輯、限制與法遵規則，結算朝原子化邁進，並將 AI 代理視為具有完整地位的交易主體。但這究竟是結構性轉變，還是換了新裝的數位化？本場開場議程將嘗試區分真正的架構與炒作，並提出關鍵問題：可程式化貨幣與代幣化金融產品，究竟能走多遠？

title: When Enterprises Buy Emerging Tech, Who Shares the Risk?
speakers: Paul Hodes; Jorden Seet; Osamu Abe; Richard Wormald; Murli Ravi
description: Enterprise buyers increasingly want emerging technology to deliver measurable business outcomes, not simply another software subscription. But before buyers and vendors can share risk, they must establish what the technology can genuinely deliver, how success will be measured, and how much depends on the buyer’s own systems, data and adoption. This session explores how enterprises distinguish a compelling demonstration from a solution worth scaling, agree verifiable performance baselines, and structure shared-risk commercial arrangements that work for both sides, including when outcome-linked commitments are unrealistic.

title: Rewiring Banking Around the Customer: From Product-Centric to Customer-Centric Organizations - Powered by SCBX
description: How AI, customer intelligence, and new operating models are rewiring financial institutions to move beyond product-centric banking toward meaningful customer engagement and better financial outcomes.

title: From Chat to Checkout: An AI Agent That Sells for You - Powered by Meta
description: Across APAC, millions of businesses already sell through messaging apps - until it's time to get paid, and the conversation stalls. Meta Business Agent closes that gap: an always-on assistant that greets customers, responds in local languages, showcases products, and collects payment, all within the chat. Join us to see how conversational commerce is reshaping how businesses in the region win and keep customers.

title: Scaling AI: Where Financial Services is Seeing Real Returns
speakers: Quan Yu; Janet Young; Abhijeet Ramesh; Mayoran Rajendra; Vish Sharma
description:
The conversation around AI in financial services has moved beyond experimentation. The challenge is no longer identifying promising use cases—it's deploying AI at scale in ways that deliver measurable business value. From payments and banking to fintech and customer engagement, leading institutions are embedding AI into core operations to improve productivity, strengthen risk management, personalise customer experiences, and accelerate innovation. Yet while some initiatives become enterprise capabilities, many others remain trapped in pilot mode.

Bringing together leaders from across the financial services ecosystem, this panel explores where AI is creating tangible impact today, what it takes to scale successful deployments across the organisation, and the operational, cultural, and governance challenges that determine whether AI delivers lasting value. The discussion will examine how institutions are prioritising AI investments, measuring success beyond productivity gains, and building the data, operating models, and organisational capabilities needed to move from isolated use cases to enterprise-wide transformation.
description_zh: 金融服務領域有關 AI 的討論已超越試驗階段。挑戰不再是找出有潛力的使用情境，而是以能帶來可衡量商業價值的方式，大規模部署 AI。從支付與銀行業務，到金融科技與客戶互動，領先機構正將 AI 嵌入核心營運，以提高生產力、強化風險管理、提供個人化客戶體驗並加速創新。然而，部分計畫雖然已成為企業能力，許多其他計畫卻仍困在試點階段。本場座談匯聚金融服務生態系各領域的領導者，探討 AI 如今在哪些方面帶來實質影響、如何將成功部署擴展至整個組織，以及哪些營運、文化與治理挑戰，決定 AI 能否創造持久價值。討論將檢視各機構如何排定 AI 投資的優先順序、如何在生產力提升之外衡量成功，以及如何建立必要的資料、營運模式與組織能力，從零散的使用情境走向全企業轉型。

title: Tokenization at Scale: From Pilot to On Chain Money Movement - Powered by J.P. Morgan
description: Tokenization is moving from pilots to production. In 15 minutes, we’ll share what corporates, asset managers, FIs and fintechs need to adopt on chain money movement: where value is real, what risks show up in production, and the operating controls that unlock scale, grounded in real-world tokenized payments and tokenized fund examples.
description_zh: 代幣化正從試點走向正式營運。在 15 分鐘內，我們將透過真實世界的代幣化支付與代幣化基金案例，分享企業、資產管理公司、金融機構與金融科技公司採用鏈上資金流動所需了解的事項：真正的價值在哪裡、正式營運時會出現哪些風險，以及哪些營運控制能促成規模化。

title: Scaling Human + AI Collaboration: From AI Pilots to Enterprise Transformation - Powered by DBS Bank
description: Most organisations have AI pilots, but few have AI at scale. This session unpacks what it takes to close that gap. That means rethinking how people and AI work together, building governance that enables rather than constrains, and making sure adoption delivers results that employees and customers can feel.

We’ll also discuss how fintechs can better serve women customers and women entrepreneurs.

Serving a Billion: What Do India's Consumer Platforms Know About Scale?

Fireside Chat - Vijay Shekhar Sharma

India's consumer platforms serve hundreds of millions of people through payments, cards, travel and financial services. Founders of leading platforms discuss how to scale adoption while building customer trust and sustainable, profitable businesses.

title: FinTech in ASEAN 2027 - From Sustainable Scale to Intelligent Growth
speakers: Luke Boland; Taka Yamada; Stephanie King-Chung Hung; Wanyi Wong
description: ASEAN's fintech industry is entering a new phase of maturity, shifting from rapid expansion towards sustainable business models, intelligent financial infrastructure and meaningful commercial impact. Artificial intelligence, digital assets, tokenisation and increasingly interconnected payment networks are transforming financial services and creating opportunities for greater efficiency and financial inclusion. Yet realising their potential requires navigating fragmented markets, evolving regulation, cybersecurity threats and growing expectations around trust and operational resilience. Against this backdrop, the FinTech in ASEAN 2027 report will examine how the region’s FinTech ecosystem is evolving, where investment and innovation are gaining momentum, and what it takes to scale across diverse ASEAN markets. It will explore the convergence of technology, capital and regulation, including the role of financial institutions, investors, regulators and technology providers in accelerating adoption and building a more connected financial ecosystem.

title: Stablecoins, Tokenized Deposits and Tokenized MMF: Which Money Earns a Place in the Stack?
speakers: Lewis Sun; Humphrey Valenbreder; Khairi Azmi; Laura Loh
description: Stablecoins, tokenized deposits and tokenized MMFs are all racing to become the default form of institutional money, though none of them do the same job equally well. Three advocates, one per instrument get two minutes each to pitch to our moderator, who presses each on the trade-offs. Then the audience votes: what would you actually hold for payroll, for treasury, for cross-border? Come find out what counts as money when the answer depends on the job.

title: HSG NextGen Agentic Banking: A Revolution in the Banking Interaction Paradigm - Powered by Hi Sun FinTech Global Limited Company
description:
This session introduces next-generation Agentic Banking to banking audiences, covering three key areas:

• Agentic Banking architecture and its evolution roadmap

• The paradigm shift in banking interaction: from App-first to AI-first

• A real-world implementation case and measurable outcomes at a native digital bank in Southeast Asia

title: Merchant Insights: Local-First, Not Card-First: Checkout Lessons from Europe and the Middle East - Presented by Coda Shop's Storefront Recharge.com & StartSelect.com
speakers: Ivan Chang; Aimun Baloch; Ameen Almohsen
description: Most global checkouts still assume everyone pays by card. Across Coda’s businesses in Europe and the Middle East, fewer than 30% come from a typed card, and in Egypt almost no one pays that way. Coda shares its stories from both regions and what merchants should build instead through our experience operating multiple storefronts in region including Recharge.com and StartSelect.com.

title: The End of Anonymous Ownership? The Next Era of On-Chain Finance - Powered by Cleanverse
description: As TradFi moves on-chain, can ownership of regulated digital assets remain anonymous? Programmed Governance offers a new model where trusted identity, asset eligibility and policy rules are checked and validated before value moves. As money becomes programmable, this session explores the next frontier: rewiring policy for an era of programmable value.
description_zh: 隨著傳統金融（TradFi）走向鏈上，受監管數位資產的所有權還能保持匿名嗎？程式化治理（Programmed Governance）提出一種新模式，在價值轉移之前先檢查並驗證可信身分、資產資格及政策規則。當貨幣變得可程式化，本場次將探索下一個前沿：為可程式化價值時代重塑政策。

title: Why Incentives Are Misaligned in Global Banking - Powered by Lorum
description: Incentives are misaligned in global banking. Large banks run networks that cannot serve today's FI volume at a viable cost, so mid-market firms turn to challenger banks that fund lending with client float. Clearing, custody and liquidity are fiduciary and belong in a 100% reserve model. Attendees leave knowing where operational money should sit.

title: From Breakthrough to Scale: Introducing the NUS-AIDF Deep FinTech Scaler Programme
From Market Entry to Regional Scale: What Does It Take to Win Across ASEAN?
speakers: Lucy Liu; Nandini Joshi; Calvin Tan; Harshet Lunani; Alvinder Singh
description: ASEAN offers significant opportunities for regional growth, but its diversity means that success in one market does not readily translate to another. For Singapore-based FinTechs, the challenge is not simply where to expand, but how to sequence that growth: build credibility with a major customer at home, or enter another market early to test whether the business can travel. Firms must also decide what to own, what to localise and where partnerships can provide faster access to customers, infrastructure and regulatory capabilities. AI may sharpen market insights and support experimentation, but its value depends on sound use cases, trusted data and effective governance. These choices ultimately determine whether expansion creates regional scale or merely complexity.

title: AI & Core Banking: Who Builds the Machine, Who Regulates it? Core Banking's New Compliance Perimeter
speakers: Celine Le Cotonnec; Will Montgomery; Jessica Rusu; Isabella Chase
description:
Core banking functions such as credit decisions, trade finance, fraud detection and KYC are shifting from pilot demonstrations into live, algorithm-driven workflows, and the institutions pulling ahead are rebuilding these processes end to end rather than adding AI on top of what already exists.

This session brings together the people actually doing that rebuild - the platforms it runs on, the institutions deploying it, and the regulators overseeing it - to work through what that rebuild actually requires: which controls move from human sign-off to automated checkpoints, and where the audit trail needs redesigning rather than retrofitting.
description_zh: 信貸決策、貿易融資、詐欺偵測及認識你的客戶（KYC）等核心銀行業務，正從試點展示轉向由演算法驅動的正式工作流程。領先的機構正在端到端重建這些流程，而不是在既有系統上附加 AI。本場次匯聚真正參與重建的人，包括支撐流程的平台、部署流程的機構及負責監督的監管機關，共同探討重建實際需要什麼：哪些控管措施要從人工簽核轉為自動化檢查點，以及哪些稽核軌跡需要重新設計，而非事後改裝。

title: Beyond the Product Stack: Platform as the New Advantage in Banking - Powered by Veefin Solutions
description: Banks have spent a decade buying products like Cash management, Trade Finance, Supply Chain Finance, Lending; and stitching them together afterwards. The cost isn't just efficiency; it caps growth: fragmented data, duplicated workflows, and change that moves at the pace of the slowest system. This session argues that banking's next competitive advantage is architectural, and shows what institutions building on one foundation do differently.

title: Liquidity Fragmentation: Tokenization's Hidden Risk - Powered by Hashgraph
description: Tokenization pilots keep succeeding technically and failing to scale, because liquidity fragments across a dozen new rails instead of moving as one. This session makes the case that fragmentation, not technology, is the real risk institutions face next, and shows what banks moving past the pilot stage are actually doing differently to solve it.
description_zh: 代幣化試點在技術上屢屢成功，卻無法擴大規模，原因是流動性分散在十多條新的基礎通道，而未能整體流動。本場次將說明，機構接下來面臨的真正風險是碎片化，而非技術，並展示已跨越試點階段的銀行實際採取了哪些不同做法來解決這個問題。

title: AI Costs Are Outpacing Outcomes: The Missing Layer in Enterprise AI - Powered by NeoSapients
description: Enterprises have piloted AI. In production, budgets run out within months as inference costs outgrow outcomes. In this presentation, we run a bank's recurring fee disputes at scale and show why: agents resend excess context and re-reason solved cases on every call. We then route them through an independent control layer and compare cost per case, accuracy and audit trail, with learning kept in-house.

title: Asia's Financial Rewiring - Who Wins, Who Gets Left Behind?
speakers: Wilson Beh; Jaclyn Tsai; Lito Villanueva; Holly Fang
description: As ASEAN's fintech ecosystem matures, a bigger question emerges: will the region's technological progress translate into lasting competitive advantage in the global financial system? The rules of competition are changing. AI is reshaping financial services, digital assets are challenging traditional infrastructure, and geopolitical realignments are redirecting capital, talent and financial flows. Meanwhile, regulatory divergence and competing national priorities are testing ambitions for greater regional integration. These shifts will create winners and losers. Some markets will emerge as centres for next-generation financial innovation and infrastructure, while others risk losing relevance. Established financial centres and business models may find their traditional advantages increasingly challenged. Bringing together presidents of leading fintech associations across Asia, this candid discussion moves beyond familiar calls for regional collaboration to examine the difficult strategic choices facing individual markets. Which competitive advantages will endure? Where will the next financial champions emerge? Can Asian economies strengthen their collective influence while competing for the same opportunities?

title: RWA Tokenization: From Products to Liquid Markets
speakers: Kazuya Ikeda; Fiona Murray; Chris Yin; Delane Foo
description: RWA tokenisation has a surplus of vision and a shortage of honest post-mortems. This session is the latter. Which asset classes are seeing real traction, and which are stuck in pilot theatre? How much settlement has actually been compressed and what breaks in the transition? Tokenised collateral promises mobility the legacy system can't match, but only if the legal frameworks hold. The question for banks, financial institutions and asset managers: who are the new investors, and what do they need to see before they allocate? Practitioners who have shipped and carry the scars, separate the working from the wished-for.
description_zh: 現實世界資產（RWA）代幣化不缺願景，缺的是坦誠的事後檢討。本場次正是這樣的檢討。哪些資產類別真正獲得市場採用，哪些仍停留在試點展示？結算時間實際縮短了多少，轉型過程又有哪些環節失靈？代幣化擔保品有望提供傳統系統無法比擬的流動能力，但前提是法律架構必須站得住腳。銀行、金融機構及資產管理業者要問的是：新投資人是誰，他們在配置資金前需要看到什麼？真正推出過產品、也承受過挫折的實務工作者，將分辨哪些做法確實有效，哪些仍只是期望。

description: As trade corridors shift and USD liquidity tightens, SMEs are moving into new markets faster than financial institutions can keep up. This session explores what's changing on the ground and how banks can support SME growth across emerging-market corridors and beyond.

title: Next-Generation Payment Infrastructure — From Real-Time Interconnection to Tokenised Settlement - Powered by Shenzhen Ylink Computing Co., Ltd
description:
Moving from real-time connectivity to tokenized settlement is not merely about “issuing tokens”; the biggest challenge is dismantling the old set of rules built around end-of-day settlement. When traditional clearing windows, reconciliation cycles, liquidity scheduling, and regulatory reporting cut-off times are completely disrupted, how should bank payment systems be re-architected?

This session will explore this in practice along the bank payment chain and focus directly on three core challenges: how a unified gateway can connect SWIFT, RTGS, fast payment systems, and mBridge; how tokenized deposits can support delivery-versus-payment (DvP) while retaining their deposit attributes; and how, once the end-of-day anchor is gone, the timing and data boundaries of regulatory reporting should be redefined.

title: When Agents Direct Agents: Who Do You Actually Regulate?
speakers: Daniela Stoffel; Mahesh Uttamchandani; Claude Marx; Kenneth Gay; Jonah Crane
description:
Financial regulation has always assumed that decisions can be traced through a clear chain of human accountability. But as AI agents begin directing other agents, that assumption starts to break down. Agentic AI won't just automate tasks—it has the potential to reshape how financial institutions are organised. Decision-making may shift between people and AI systems, reporting lines become more fluid, and the traditional structures underpinning governance, accountability and supervision begin to evolve. In that world, who is ultimately responsible for a decision? What exactly is a regulator supervising?

Bringing together senior policymakers and regulators, this session explores how supervisory frameworks—from senior manager accountability regimes to board oversight and the three lines of defence—need to adapt for organisations where humans increasingly govern systems that, in turn, govern other systems. The discussion will examine how institutions can demonstrate accountability, maintain effective oversight, and provide regulators with meaningful traceability in increasingly agent-driven operating models. Rather than focusing on individual AI decisions, the panel asks a broader question: how should governance evolve when the organisation itself becomes dynamic?
description_zh: 金融監管一直假設，決策可以沿著清楚的人類責任鏈追溯。然而，隨著 AI 代理開始指揮其他代理，這項假設正逐漸失效。代理型 AI 不只會自動化任務，也可能重塑金融機構的組織方式。決策權可能在人員與 AI 系統之間移轉，匯報關係變得更具流動性，支撐治理、問責及監理的傳統結構也開始演變。在這樣的世界裡，誰對決策負最終責任？監管機關究竟在監督什麼？本場次匯聚資深政策制定者與監管者，探討從高階主管問責制度、董事會監督到三道防線的監理架構，應如何因應這類組織：人類愈來愈多地治理系統，而系統又治理其他系統。討論將檢視，在日益由代理驅動的營運模式中，機構如何證明責任歸屬、維持有效監督，並向監管機關提供有實質意義的可追溯性。本場論壇不只聚焦個別 AI 決策，更提出一個廣泛的問題：當組織本身變得動態，治理應如何演進？

title: Who Owns the Moment an Agent Decides to Pay?
speakers: Roseate Wagner; Crystal Bryant-Minter; Adit Gadgil; Vijeth Pandit; Nagesh Jaladi
description: Your next customer won't be human. AI agents are becoming first-class transactors — browsing, deciding and paying with no person in the loop. When software initiates the payment, the contest shifts from the rail to the moment of intent: who owns it — the wallet, the platform, the merchant, or the agent's operator? What does an agent need before it can spend: identity, mandate, limits, recourse? Why do stablecoins and programmable money fit machine-initiated commerce better than card rails built for humans? And when an agent pays the wrong party on the wrong instruction, who is liable? The checkout is being rebuilt for machines. This session is about who gets to own it.
description_zh: 你的下一位客戶將不是人類。AI 代理正在成為獨立的交易主體，在無人介入的情況下瀏覽、決策及付款。當付款由軟體發起，競爭焦點便從支付通道轉向意圖形成的那一刻：究竟由誰掌握，是錢包、平台、商家，還是代理的營運者？代理在支出前需要哪些條件：身分、授權、限額及追索途徑？為什麼穩定幣與可程式化貨幣比為人類設計的卡片支付通道，更適合由機器發起的商業活動？當代理依據錯誤指令付款給錯誤對象時，又該由誰承擔責任？結帳流程正為機器重新打造。本場次探討誰能掌握這個環節。

title: Digital Autonomy in AI: Optionality Over Absolute Independence
speakers: Steven Maijoor; Dr. Joseph Breeden; Prof. Dr. Fritzi Köhler-Geib; Sunayna Tuteja
description:
No bank can or should build every AI capability itself. The real strategic question isn't build versus buy; it's whether institutions retain meaningful choice over the technology they depend on. As agentic AI begins making decisions that affect customers, capital, and risk, financial institutions must ask: How much digital dependency is acceptable? Can they trust and explain the decision of models they didn't build? What happens when the AI underpinning critical operations is controlled by a single provider?

The panel explores what digital autonomy should look like in the AI era. Rather than arguing for complete self-sufficiency, the discussion focuses on optionality: the ability to choose between providers, maintain control over sensitive data, satisfy regulatory expectations for explainability, and preserve resilient fallback options when business or technology priorities change. The conversation will examine how banks can adopt AI at scale without sacrificing transparency, governance or strategic independence - and why genuine optionality may become one of the industry's most important competitive advantages.
description_zh: 沒有一家銀行能夠或應該自行打造所有 AI 能力。真正的策略問題不是自建或採購，而是機構是否對其所依賴的技術保有實質選擇權。隨著代理型 AI 開始做出影響客戶、資本及風險的決策，金融機構必須問：多大程度的數位依賴可以接受？對於並非自行建立的模型所做的決策，是否能夠信任並加以解釋？當支撐關鍵營運的 AI 由單一供應商控制時，會發生什麼事？本場論壇探討 AI 時代的數位自主應有何種樣貌。討論不以完全自給自足為訴求，而是聚焦選擇空間：能在供應商之間選擇、維持對敏感資料的控制、滿足監管機關對可解釋性的期待，以及在業務或技術優先順序改變時，保留具有韌性的備援選項。對話將檢視銀行如何在不犧牲透明度、治理或策略獨立性的前提下，大規模採用 AI，以及為何真正的選擇權可能成為業界最重要的競爭優勢之一。

description_zh: 代幣化失敗的原因不是願景，而是底層基礎設施。每一條正式運作的走廊背後，都有一套不起眼卻決定其能否擴大規模的技術架構。該選擇哪種結算層：L1、L2 還是私有鏈，又各有什麼取捨？如何在意見不一致的司法管轄區之間達成法律上的最終性？哪些互通標準真正重要，又由誰推動？本場次將解析案例研究背後可複製的組成要素，探討哪些決策讓系統得以正式投入生產，而不只是昂貴的概念驗證。

title: When Growth Gets Harder, What Must a Company Simplify to Keep Scaling in 2027?
speakers: Prajit Nanu; Rob Schimek; Vince Iswara; Suresh Shankar
description: Bigger teams do not automatically build more valuable companies. In its H1 2024 results, Klarna reported a 73% increase in revenue per employee, citing AI-driven efficiencies alongside business growth. But greater efficiency is not the same as sustainable scale. This session explores what companies must simplify to keep growing in 2027: which workflows to automate, what to standardise across markets, where human domain expertise remains indispensable, and which specialised hires still warrant investment. The conversation tests when restructuring unlocks growth and when it strips out essential capability. What should leaders remove, redesign or protect so the business becomes easier to scale, not merely cheaper to run?

title: Agentic Payments: Are Our Rails Ready?
speakers: Jesse McWaters; Jeremy Goro; Kelvin Li; Jo Yeo
description:
For decades, payment systems have been designed around human behaviour. AI agents could upend those assumptions. Unlike humans, agents do not care about rewards, interfaces or brand loyalty. They optimise for speed, cost, reliability and programmability. As agents begin making payments on behalf of users and businesses, they may transact at a scale and frequency never seen before — and they will do so without the friction, loyalty, and psychology that payment systems have long relied upon to manage risk and drive behaviour.

This raises three questions. Can machines be trusted to make payments using our rails — and who is accountable when something goes wrong? Can agents genuinely serve users and merchants better than today's systems, or do they simply add a layer of opacity between people and their money? And what does the next generation of payment infrastructure need to look like to make agentic commerce safe, inclusive, and scalable? As PayNow Generation 2 considers capabilities relevant to agentic commerce, this session tackles all three.

This panel brings together the networks, national payment schemes, policymakers and multilateral hubs working to make cross-border payments more connected, examining where regulatory and commercial frictions persist, how different payment ecosystems can connect and scale across markets, and what smaller or newer markets need to participate on viable terms.

title: Balance Sheet Strategy in Money 3.0
speakers: Tristan Kirchner; Nischint Sanghavi; Kirit Bhatia; George Davis; Olivia Marzuki
description: For CFOs and treasurers, programmable money is not a thesis, it's an allocation decision. Where does settlement risk really sit when value moves in real time, and who carries the exposure? How does tokenisation rewrite collateral management and intraday liquidity? What does the yield/risk trade-off look like across deposits and other forms of money, and what happens to deposit insurance and the lender of last resort when money is code? The question boards are starting to ask: whose balance sheet does each instrument sit on, yours, your bank's, or nobody's? And are balance sheet light banking models the safer answer? A working session for the people who answer with real money.
description_zh: 對財務長及財務主管而言，可程式化貨幣不是一套論述，而是資金配置決策。當價值即時移轉，結算風險究竟存在於哪裡，又由誰承擔曝險？代幣化如何改變擔保品管理及日內流動性？存款與其他貨幣形式之間的收益與風險取捨如何？當貨幣化為程式碼，存款保險及最後貸款人制度又會如何？董事會開始提出的問題是：每種工具究竟列在誰的資產負債表上，是你自己的、你的銀行的，還是不屬於任何人？而輕資產負債表的銀行模式，是否是更安全的答案？這是一場為必須以真金白銀作答的人設計的實務討論。

title: Financing Financial Infrastructure in Emerging Markets
speakers: Hon. Ebson Uanguta; Dr. Shaji Krishnan V; T. S. Shankar
description:
Building the infrastructure for financial inclusion and cross-border connectivity is one challenge. Financing it is another, and it's the one that usually gets skipped over in the excitement about what could be built. Is the binding constraint on financial inclusion the technology, or the capital to build and sustain it?

This panel brings together leaders from a small economy building its own digital public infrastructure, a hub positioning itself to draw global capital into a fast-growing regional market, and a development bank whose entire mandate is getting credit to populations mainstream finance still doesn't reach. The dialogue will focus on where the funding for this actually comes from, state budgets, development finance, or private capital drawn in by the right market positioning, and what it takes for a smaller or developing market to make itself genuinely investable.
description_zh: 建置普惠金融與跨境互聯的基礎設施是一項挑戰，為它籌措資金則是另一項。而每當人們熱烈討論可以建造什麼時，資金問題往往被略過。制約普惠金融的關鍵究竟是技術，還是建置並維持運作所需的資本？本場論壇匯聚多方領導者：正在打造自身數位公共基礎設施的小型經濟體、致力吸引全球資本進入快速成長區域市場的樞紐，以及以向主流金融仍未觸及的人群提供信貸為使命的開發銀行。對話將聚焦這些資金實際從何而來，包括國家預算、開發融資，或透過適當市場定位吸引的民間資本，以及較小型或發展中市場需要具備哪些條件，才能真正成為值得投資的對象。

title: Can Technology Make Every Small Business Bankable?
speakers: Alon Eitan; Dr. Dmytro Kolechko; Suttipong Kanakakorn; Matthias Kröner
description:
Millions of viable small businesses remain underserved not because they lack economic activity, but because traditional financial systems struggle to see, assess and serve them efficiently. As AI, alternative data, digital lending and transaction-banking infrastructure improve, can financial institutions build a fundamentally different model for SME finance?

This session explores how financial institutions can use richer business data to understand SMEs, automate credit and working-capital decisions, and build scalable digital infrastructure that lowers the cost of serving smaller businesses. It will examine what is already working, what still prevents these models from scaling, and whether the next phase of financial inclusion will come not from creating more financial products, but from making previously invisible businesses visible and bankable.

title: Unlocking AI Value in Financial Services - Powered by Infosys
description: AI is now table stakes in banking. Most banks run the same fraud, KYC and onboarding use cases, yet few can show their board a hard return. Drawing on recent global research with banking leaders and hands-on experience with banks across Asia Pacific and beyond, this session explains why most still pay full price for every new AI initiative. It then sets out three shifts that make each deployment faster and cheaper than the last, turning AI from a cost centre into a compounding asset.

title: Geoeconomics of Tokens: Lessons From Live Cross-Border Tokenized Corridors
speakers: Oli Harris; Alan Lim; Scott Bauguess; Niki Ariyasinghe; Angela Ang
description: Cross-border tokenized corridors are moving from proof-of-concept to production. Hear from the people who made the crossing: what broke first - tech, legal or liquidity; what the operating model actually looks like when someone has to issue, settle and supervise; what they would never build again; and the honest timeline from pilot to scaled corridor. This discussion will be around the gating factors, the requirements, and what it really takes to move live value across borders on tokenised rails.
description_zh: 跨境代幣化走廊正從概念驗證邁向正式運作。聽聽已跨越這道門檻的人分享：最先出問題的是技術、法律還是流動性；當有人必須負責發行、結算及監督時，實際營運模式是什麼樣貌；哪些東西他們絕不會再打造一次；以及從試點走向具規模走廊的真實時程。這場討論將聚焦關鍵制約因素、必要條件，以及透過代幣化基礎通道跨境移轉真實價值究竟需要什麼。

title: How to Evaluate a Strategic Exit vs. Continuing to Build?
speakers: Rahul Shinghal; Benjamin Fernandes; Michael Stemmle; Kaweewut Temphuwapat; Navin Suri
description: With conventional IPO pathways narrowed and growth-stage liquidity constrained, many companies must re-evaluate what a successful outcome looks like. Crunchbase's 2026 M&A Outlook recorded 36 unicorn M&A exits worth a combined $67B in 2025, and EY-Parthenon reports teams under 100 people landing $100M+ acqui-hire exits. An early acqui-hire or IP sale can preserve talent and technological value, but requires careful negotiation. This session outlines the operational indicators and timing indicators founders need to weigh a structured exit against continuing to build.
description_zh: 隨著傳統首次公開募股（IPO）途徑收窄，成長階段企業的流動性受限，許多公司必須重新評估何謂成功的結果。Crunchbase 的《2026 年併購展望》記錄了 2025 年 36 起獨角獸企業透過併購退出的交易，總值達 670 億美元；EY-Parthenon 則指出，少於 100 人的團隊也能透過人才收購取得逾 1 億美元的退出成果。及早進行人才收購或出售智慧財產權，可以保留人才及技術價值，但需要謹慎協商。本場次將說明創辦人在衡量有規劃的退出與繼續打造事業之間，應考慮哪些營運及時機指標。

This conversation explores how to bridge that gap: what must change in operating models, architecture and workflows; how cloud infrastructure can support deployment at scale; and how to manage orchestration, guardrails and human oversight without slowing progress. It will also examine where agents deliver real efficiency today, where returns remain uncertain, and why so many projects struggle to scale.

title: SFA FinTech Talent Report 2026: Building Singapore's Next FinTech Talent Advantage
speakers: Hassan Ahmed; Tawishi Singh; Anitta Krishan; Wei Lun Tan; Jonathan Goldstein
description:
The SFA FinTech Talent Report 2026, produced by SFA with Page Executive, finds Singapore's next fintech advantage will be built on talent. The priority is to develop and mobilise a workforce that can take innovation beyond experimentation to commercialisation, institutional adoption and global scale.

As artificial intelligence, tokenisation, and digital assets redefine financial services, the industry's competitive advantage is shifting from access to capital and technology towards the ability to attract, develop, and retain future-ready talent.

This report finds that while fintech hiring remains resilient, the nature of demand is changing dramatically. Employers are actively seeking AI specialists, cybersecurity experts, product leaders, risk and compliance professionals, and commercial executives capable of translating innovation into growth. Yet the most sought-after talent is not purely technical. It is individuals who can operate at the intersection of technology, business, and regulation which is an increasingly scarce combination in today's market.

A recurring theme throughout the report is the emergence of a new talent paradox: organisations have access to larger talent pools, yet struggle to find candidates with the capabilities required for an AI-enabled future. The challenge is no longer a shortage of people, but a shortage of skills, adaptability, and leadership.

The report highlights four defining trends shaping the future of the workforce: AI reshaping work; the apprenticeship model under pressure as automation absorbs many entry-level tasks; evolving leadership expectations; and continuous reinvention as a career requirement.

The report also examines how internships, graduate programmes, career conversion pathways, and cross-industry talent mobility will play a critical role in strengthening Singapore's talent pipeline. It highlights the importance of collaboration between employers, educational institutions, and policymakers in ensuring the workforce evolves as quickly as the industry itself.

Ultimately, the future of fintech will not be determined by technology alone. The organisations that lead the next decade will be those that build workforces capable of adapting, innovating, and thriving amid constant change.

title: Building Trust Together: A Trust Network for Agentic AI
description: Agentic Al is evolving rapidly, and organisations demand governance and control to stay safe. Verifiable agent identities, protected data access, inference guardrails, and auditable records of action are key ingredients to operate with accountability, but no single solution exists today. In this session, Terminal 3 and Affinidi present their shared vision of how confidential computing, verifiable agent identity, options for secure inference, and immutable audit records will allow agentic workflows that cross departments, cross organisations, and cross the world. Hear their perspective of how enterprises and developers can accelerate safe agentic growth by adopting this advanced technology based on open standards.

title: Building Trusted Hubs for Programmable Money
speakers: Rene Michau; Hon. Natia Turnava; Peter Loo; James Boey
description:
As rules move into the money itself, the appeal of a jurisdiction or a platform depends less on legacy and more on whether innovators, institutions and regulators can all trust what is built on it. Earning that trust rests on three tests.

First, clarity: rules that are predictable enough for firms to commit capital and talent, and robust enough to protect stability.

Second, connectivity: rails that link new forms of money to the traditional financial system and across borders, so that value created in one market can move into others.

Third, credibility: compliance that holds up across jurisdictions, because a hub is only as strong as the standards its participants carry abroad.

The panel will discuss what makes a jurisdiction or platform a trusted home for programmable money, where programmable money is delivering value today, and how regulators and industry can build hubs that are open to innovation and trusted for stability.

title: [Booth 4A25] Coffee & Conversations: The Premium Wood Card
description: Join Atul Singh, Global Head of Distribution Sales at G+D, and Ashwini Pandey, CEO of Copecto, for an exclusive showcase of premium wood payment cards over coffee. Discover the craftsmanship and possibilities of premium wood cards, exchange ideas, and connect with industry experts to discuss the future of premium card experiences.

title: [Booth 2A13] Happy Hour
description:
Join us for happy hour at the AWS booth!

Wrap your day at Singapore Fintech with the AWS team! Stop by the AWS booth for a happy hour, where you can unwind and connect over drinks. We look forward to raising a glass with you.

title: SME Finance Forum Community Meeting
speakers: Qamar Saleem; Samantha Sangster; Mark Barnett; Dr. Vincent Zheng; Paula Pelaez; John David Yap; Sumit Khurana; Ashraf Abdelfattah; Innocent Enock Yonazi; Sopnendu Mohanty
description:
The SME Finance Forum (SMEFF) was established in 2012 by the G20 and is managed by the World Bank Group. Our objective is to scale SME finance for job creation and economic growth. As the leading SME finance network globally, we steer industry innovations, support replication of best practices, steer policy advocacy, and foster global knowledge transfer. We also power our global peer learning membership network by connecting them with relevant partners, investors and policymakers.

This session highlights the SME Finance Forum's (SMEFF) transformation journey, showcasing key achievements and strategic priorities developed. Get an insider's view of SMEFF's latest milestones from the last 12 months and contribute to shaping the future initiatives meant to solve the MSME finance gap.

Join an interactive conversation with SME Finance Forum members, affiliates, and partners as they share experiences, insights, and lessons from across the global SME finance ecosystem. Through audience participation and open dialogue, attendees will have the opportunity to discuss emerging challenges, identify opportunities for collaboration, and help shape the Forum's future priorities. The session will conclude with an interactive Q&A.
