description: How regulated businesses can deliver great AI-powered customer experiences while staying safe, secure, and compliant.

title: The Next Wave of Innovators
speakers: David Symington; Mynard Mojica; Kaustuva Dipta Pany; Fonteneau Annabelle; Alex Panican
description:
The next wave of innovation, disruption, and impact is driven by startups building with frontier tech and agility.

This session showcases the winning solutions and startups from GFTN's supported programmes.

The Luxembourg House of Financial Technology (LHoFT)’s Catapult: Inclusion SE Asia will showcase a winning fintech driving financial inclusion and social impact in Southeast Asia.

ASEAN Financial Health Challenge, an initiative by GFTN and Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), with UNSGSA as a Thematic Thought Partner, will showcase a representative moving the needle in financial health among individuals.

Lastly, BharatNetra Startup Accelerator will showcase a startup which has progressed beyond borders from Odisha, India.

title: From Disruptor to Financial Powerhouse: The Leadership Journey of Scaling Fintechs
description: What does it take to transform from 0 to 1 start-up versus 1 to 100 scale-up? This fireside chat explores the leadership challenges of scaling a fintech—from navigating uncertainty and competitive pressures to evolving the product, culture and governance on the path to profitability & beyond. We’ll examine the complexities of international expansion while preserving a company's distinctive identity, and the human side of leadership: how different leadership styles can succeed, and how professional CEOs can build on a founder’s vision while charting their own course.

title: Project Danu: A Technical Deep Dive into Digital Twins for Climate Risk Management (By Invitation Only – Public Sector Participants)
description:
BIS Innovation Hub recently completed Project Danu, which delivered the concept of a digital twin framework for managing climate-related financial risks for the public sector. In this closed-door, by invitation only workshop, the project team will provide a deep dive into the technical design, architecture and features of the Danu prototype, and demonstrate how the prototype could be utilised.

Invitation is open to public sector participants only. For registration, please contact Carmen Arias (email: Carmen.Arias@bisih.org) and Lucy Wong (email: Lucy.Wong@bisih.org)

title: [Booth 5F25] From licence to scale: How regulation can enable trusted fintech innovation
description: Fireside chat "From licence to scale: How regulation can enable trusted fintech innovation" - Speakers: Lawrence Buka, Chief Compliance Officer at PIPO Luxembourg (subsidiary of ByteDance) and Olivier Hoen, Chief Executive Officer at PIPO Luxembourg (subsidiary of ByteDance)

title: [Booth 5F25] AML Compliance: When tech and legal come together
description: Fireside chat "AML Compliance: When tech and legal come together" - Speakers: Iain Armstrong, Executive Director at FCC Strategy, ComplyAdvantage and Anida Mumzdic, Attorney at Schiltz & Schiltz

title: [Booth 2A49] Build Clean Finance: Cleanverse Builder Session
description:
A hands-on session for developers building compliant on-chain finance. Regulators and institutions are coming on-chain, and they need apps that know who is transacting and enforce the rules on every transfer. Cleanverse gives builders that layer as simple APIs: Cleanverse Verified Identity (CVI) for wallet-bound KYC/KYB credentials, and Cleanverse Verified Assets (CVA) for tokens whose transfers are checked on-chain. Our engineers will walk through the protocol, showcase what hackathon builders have shipped with it, and live-build a compliant transfer on testnet. Bring a laptop. Attendees who complete the session can claim an on-chain attendance badge.

Agenda: Why compliance is a builder primitive · Cleanverse API walkthrough · Ecosystem keynote · Hackathon showcase · Live build · Attendance badge

Who should attend: smart contract and dApp developers, hackathon builders, students, and chain ecosystem teams.

title: Fintech Has Scaled. Now Comes the Hard Part.
speakers: Amrish Rau; Dr. Ayesha Khanna; Prajit Nanu; Rahul Shinghal; Pat Patel
description: The first decade of fintech was about proving that technology could disrupt financial services. The next is about building companies that can survive scale: navigating regulation, capital intensity, increasingly crowded markets, global expansion and the shift from payments products to full financial platforms and/or geographic expansion. Five founders and CEOs who have built fintech businesses across Asia and beyond debate what really separates a fintech that gets big from one that becomes indispensable.

title: [Booth 2C25] From Individual Awareness to Industry-Wide Defense Japan's Digital Asset AML Initiative and Opportunities for APAC Collaboration
description:
・In digital asset transactions, risks spread across borders and institutions, making the full picture difficult to see from a single firm’s data alone

・Introduces multi-layered risk assessment, monitoring across pre-transaction, post-transaction and token flows, cross-institutional risk signals, and the future AML Joint Center concept

・Seeks audience input on challenges across APAC, what information can be shared, and which stakeholders to engage

title: Rewiring Global Capital: Unlocking the Next Wave of Growth
speakers: Abror Mirzo Olimov; Katsumi Hatao; Will Oswald; Michael Schlein; Neil Parekh
description:
Capital is on the move. Changing interest rates, shifting trade ties and the growth of private markets are leading investors to rethink where they put their money. At the same time, fast-growing companies in Asia and other emerging markets want to expand abroad. Capital alone will not get them there. They need the right investors, partners and regulators on their side.

This session brings together views from leaders representing central banking, a sovereign wealth fund, fintech investing and inclusive finance. The panel will explore where the best opportunities lie today, what growth companies need to scale across borders, how good regulation builds investor confidence, and how AI is changing the way deals are made.

title: From AI Innovation to Institutional Adoption: Bridging the Gap in Financial Services
description: As AI continues to transform financial services, promising solutions still face significant barriers to institutional adoption, from technology risk management and regulatory requirements to enterprise procurement and commercial deployment. This session explores the challenges AI solution providers face in bringing their technologies to financial institutions, and introduces the AIDF Digital Finance Scaler, developed in collaboration with GFTN, as an initiative designed to bridge these gaps through institutional readiness support, technical expertise and curated industry connectivity, accelerating the journey from innovation to commercial adoption.

title: [Booth 2E13] UOI: Building the Next Generation Insurance Experience | Bringing Insurance Closer to You
description:
Discover how Artificial Intelligence (AI) could transform the insurance claims experience, making it faster, simpler and more seamless for both customers and insurers. Customers get to experience how AI could simplify claims submission, guide users through the process and provide greater clarity on their claims journey.

Step into the shoes of a claims executive and explore how AI could assist in reviewing documents, analysing claim details and recommending next steps. By reducing manual processes and supporting more informed decision-making, AI has the potential to empower claims professionals to focus on what matters most.

Embrace the future of insurance with faster, smarter and more customer-centric outcomes.

title: [Booth 2G25] Horizon: moments that matter
description: Learn how proactive, long-horizon agents that work over weeks or months, and across channels and systems, can drive your growth.

title: A Multi-Rail Future: What Should Come First?
speakers: Piero Cipollone; H.E. Chea Serey; H.E. Sheikh Ahmed bin Khalid Al-Thani; Swaminathan Janakiraman; Leong Sing Chiong; Maha El Dimachki
description:
We are moving towards a multi-rail, multi-money world, where different forms of money and payment systems coexist. Interoperability matters, but so do the integrity and resilience of the financial system. How can policymakers advance these priorities together, and are there trade-offs to be made?

This session examines what it will take to build a trusted multi-rail financial system, and whether interoperability, inclusion, consumer protection and resilience can advance together — or whether some priorities must come first. With financial systems developing at different speeds across markets, the discussion asks where policymakers should focus their efforts today to deliver the greatest benefits for users and businesses.

title: From One Tap to No Tap: The Future of Frictionless Payments
speakers: Ramakrishnan TG; Kian Teck Soh; Minsook Cho; Derek Chan
description:
Payments have become faster and easier, but the journey to make a payment is not always seamless. Online payment journeys can still involve multiple steps, from moving between apps to saving and uploading QR codes. As part of PayNow Gen2, new capabilities such as deep-linking are being explored to reduce these frictions by creating a more direct path from checkout to payment.

The next frontier could go further still. Advances in AI are opening up the possibility of agents that can search, select and transact on behalf of users. This shifts the payment experience from reducing the steps a user takes to reducing the need for users to initiate individual payments at all. This will require not only new approaches to authorisation, control and accountability, but also infrastructure capable of supporting new forms of automated payment activity, including the proposed FAST-Lite micropayments rail.

This session traces that evolution from making today's payment journeys more seamless to preparing for a future in which payments may increasingly be autonomous. It asks how the industry can continue reducing friction while preserving the control, accountability and trust that consumers and merchants expect from the payment system.

title: The Philippine FinTech Stack: Opportunities and Infrastructure Gaps for Founders and Investors
description: The Philippines has seen growing adoption of digital financial services, but gaps in core infrastructure continue to constrain the growth and economics of fintech businesses. Drawing on Kaya Founders’ The Philippine Fintech Stack 2026, this session explores the underlying challenges across identity, payments, banking access, and financial data, and the opportunities these gaps create for the next generation of fintech companies. It offers founders and investors a closer look at the infrastructure needs and market dynamics shaping the future of fintech in the Philippines.

title: The Europe Opportunities: GFTN in Europe Briefing
description: Join us as we share about the Europe FinTech landscape and what to expect in 2027.

description: A short fireside chat at the Hydra X booth for firms looking at Vietnam’s digital asset market. With Nicole Nguyen, Founder, APAC DAO.

title: From Market Entry to Revenue: Making GTM Work
description:
In this session, Hear from Christina Lim, Melanie Tschugmall and Melanie Lennert opens up why scaling and market entry are decisions that sit with the CEO, not with sales.

Get insights from a real-life client story: where the expansion broke, what it cost, what the CEO changed, and where the business stood twelve months after that.

Built for CEOs, CROs, COOs and CFOs of companies that are scaling, entering new markets, or going through an acquisition.

Leave the room after this 60-mins session:

Where expansion breaks - Early signals leadership misses

Running GTM as a system, not a function - How strategy, market selection, sales and delivery connects

Clear read on your own GTM - Know which part of your GTM will be put to test in the next market you enter

description: Fireside Chat "Agentic AI and the role of humans" - Speakers: Shash Gupta, Founder of Altcoin Buzz and Luc Maquil, Managing Partner at MAQIT

title: [Booth 3C39] Know Your Merchant: Onboarding Trust at Scale
description: Faster merchant onboarding shouldn't mean compromising on trust. Discover how intelligent KYB and digital verification help businesses streamline merchant onboarding, establish business authenticity, and reduce fraud risks while delivering a frictionless experience.

title: From AI Capability to Economic Growth
description: This week’s theme is the coming rewiring of the financial system: new risks, new rules, new growth. This fireside explores where AI’s returns are really showing up: inside companies, in the finance function, and in the broader economy. Drawing on what Stripe sees across the businesses it serves, and on research from Stripe Economics, the discussion examines why productivity gains don’t automatically become growth, how AI should change the way finance works, and what it takes for AI agents to become autonomous participants in the economy with accountability and trust.

title: Fundable by Design: How Cash Discipline Makes You a Better Bet
description:
Every founder is told to grow fast and raise big. Fewer are told that investors quietly reward the opposite: the founder who knows their runway to the week, can explain every dollar, and never pitches from desperation.

In this session, Varun Mittal argues that cash discipline is not a constraint on ambition. It is the most underrated fundraising strategy there is. Drawing on his experience as part of the founding management teams that scaled Singlife and helloPay through to acquisition, and on building an investment fund to back Singapore’s fintech community, he looks at fundraising from both sides of the table.

He shares what builds conviction in the room, the signals that end investor conversations early, and the habits that separate a good bet from a risky one, from runway planning and unit economics to how cash is managed between rounds. The result is a company that raises when it chooses to, on terms it can negotiate, and not because it has to.

Attendees will leave with a practical framework for building financial rigour into the business from day one, and a clearer view of how to become fundable by design.

title: The New Economics Across the Payments Value Chain
speakers: Anuj Khosla; Yukinobu Saeki; Shinichiro Nishikawa; Irina Chuchkina
description: For years, payments competed on the rails—faster, cheaper, more reliable ways to move money from A to B. But as transactions become instant, ubiquitous, and nearly free, the rails themselves are commoditizing. The value is migrating elsewhere: to data, embedded experiences, working capital, fraud intelligence, and the software wrapped around every transaction. Moving money is table stakes; the real margin lives above it. Learn where payments value is genuinely being created as core processing commoditizes, how leading players monetize data, software, and embedded finance beyond the transaction, and what it takes to climb the value stack.
description_zh: 多年來，支付競爭聚焦於基礎通道，設法更快速、更便宜且更可靠地把資金從 A 點移到 B 點。但隨著交易變得即時、無所不在且幾乎免費，通道本身正走向同質化。價值正轉往其他地方：資料、嵌入式體驗、營運資金、詐欺情報，以及環繞每筆交易的軟體。移轉資金只是基本門檻，真正的利潤存在於更上層的服務。了解核心處理服務同質化時，支付價值究竟在哪裡創造、領先業者如何在交易之外將資料、軟體及嵌入式金融轉化為收入，以及如何向價值鏈上層攀升。

Join us at the Catalyst Stage to witness the launch of a series of strategic partnerships that bring together public and private sector stakeholders leveraging digital innovation to address shared challenges across supply chain decarbonisation, sustainable finance and trusted climate data.

title: The Next Phase of Singapore's Green 100 National Movement
description:
Singapore’s decarbonisation ambitions hinge on mobilising its value chains, where a significant share of emissions resides. Yet for many companies, the business case for sustainability remains unclear, with fragmented reporting requirements, resource constraints and limited commercial incentives. Launched by the Council for a Competitive Climate Transition (C3T), Green 100 aims to bridge this gap by aligning buyers and suppliers around a common nationwide credential and translating sustainability efforts into tangible business opportunities.

Singapore’s Ambassador for Climate Action and Co-Chair of C3T, Mr Ravi Menon, will reflect on Green 100’s progress since its launch in May 2026 and unveil the next phase of the Green 100 national journey, strengthening the link between sustainability action, enterprise recognition and tangible business opportunities across Singapore’s supply chains.

title: Show, Don’t Forecast: What Quantum Computers Are Doing Right Now
speakers: Prof. Harry Buhrman; Julian Tan; Dr. Sua Yong Meng; Charlie Markham
description: Every quantum conversation drifts toward the 2030s. This one stays in the present tense. Quantum builders explain what their machines and methods are doing this year for financial institutions: what is in production, what is in pilots, where classical computing remains essential, and what an institution can test in the next quarter.

title: A Multi-Rail Future, Part II: Making Many Monies Work Together
speakers: Filianingsih Hendarta; Tommaso Mancini-Griffoli; Jonathan Greenstein; Maha El Dimachki
description:
The financial system is evolving towards a world where different forms of money coexist and move across increasingly interconnected networks. Fiat money and commercial bank deposits continue to underpin the global financial system, while new forms and representations of money — including tokenized deposits, payment stablecoins and central bank digital currencies — are introducing different characteristics, capabilities and ways of transacting. As traditional finance, with its established institutions, infrastructure and scale, intersects with a growing decentralised finance ecosystem, the challenge is to ensure these different forms of money and financial systems can work together.

Building on the morning’s discussion of what should come first, this panel turns to the practical realities of a multi-money, multi-rail world. How can different forms of money connect across traditional and decentralised financial systems? What infrastructure, standards and regulatory approaches are needed to enable interoperability across borders, while safeguarding monetary sovereignty, financial stability and trust?

title: Building The Trust Layer For Digital Finance - Powered by Shanghai Guan An Information Technology Co.,Ltd
description:
Digital assets and cross-border finance are rewiring the financial system, but every new rail creates new seams for attackers. Drawing on front-line experience and cases including the Binance hot-wallet breach, estimated at US$6.3 billion, David Zeng of Guan An Information maps five critical seams: identity, keys and signing, code, AI agents and cross-border data.

He shows how new rules in Singapore, the EU and China converge on three demands: know your data, prove your controls, and detect and report fast. The talk then explains how AI-driven security meets these demands in practice, covering sensitive data discovery, data masking, audit and tracing, security operations, deepfake detection, threat deception, code auditing and AI governance.

Attendees will leave with a practical three-step roadmap, visible, controllable and traceable, for financial institutions and digital asset platforms seeking to scale safely across borders. When new risks and new rules are managed well, sustainable new growth follows.

title: Merchant Insights - How Gamers Pay and Play: Insights from the Companies Serving Players Worldwide
description: Join industry veterans from Ubisoft, HoYoverse and NetEase for an inside look at where payments meet gaming. From building direct-to-consumer webshops to navigating hyper-local payment preferences across global markets, discover the payment strategies and infrastructure powering some of the world’s most-played games.

title: [Booth 2E13] NTU: Startup Showcase - Pints AI, Synvo AI
description:
Discover how two NTU-supported startups are tackling some of the biggest challenges in enterprise AI adoption. Join the founders of Pints AI and Synvo AI as they showcase innovative solutions designed to help organisations move beyond AI experimentation and achieve real business impact.

Pints AI will share how regulated industries can deploy compliant, accurate and auditable AI agents at scale, while Synvo AI will demonstrate how enterprise AI can securely capture and reuse organisational knowledge, decisions and expertise. Together, these startups offer a glimpse into the next generation of AI systems built for business.

title: [Booth 2C25] AI-Native Financial Operations and Generative AI for Legacy Migration
description:
・As financial institutions face labor shortages and a shrinking pool of skilled professionals, there is growing demand to embed AI into both operations and system development.

・This seminar presents Hitachi’s approach to AI adoption with financial institutions — applying AI agents to lending and inheritance, and regenerating design documents from legacy mainframes using generative AI.

title: The Collective Business of Going Green: Insights from Singapore's Green 100 National Movement
speakers: Lim Tuang Liang; Taichi Murakami; Clara Kwan; Andy Teo Chek Peng; Lee Bing Yi
description:
For businesses, particularly SMEs in value and supply chains, the case for sustainability is often difficult to translate into action. Costs and complexity are immediate while commercial benefits tend to feel distant and uncertain.

Singapore’s Green 100 movement seeks to change the equation. By converging government agencies, trade associations, financial institutions and the private sector around common pathways, Green 100 makes sustainability simpler to start, scale, and unlock value for businesses that take action.

The launch of Green 100 Bronze marks an important shift from recognition to reward. Procurement is singled out as the first major “value unlock”, with Singapore’s public and private sectors working to harmonise recognition of Green 100 in supplier selection and incentivisation. What will it take to translate such recognition into sustained market demand? And how can green procurement be reinforced by green financing, market access, grants, and other economic incentives?

Singapore’s 2027 ASEAN chairmanship also raises a wider opportunity. Are there Green 100 learnings that other ASEAN Member States can leverage? Which elements – common pathways, trusted credentials, “queen bee” mobilisation, or value unlocks – can be replicated in other markets? And could these different national approaches become increasingly interoperable over time?

This panel brings together leaders from the government, business, procurement and finance sectors to examine the choices, challenges, and next steps for Green 100; and how Singapore’s experience might contribute to broader activation of the ASEAN green economy.

title: Pay It Forward
description: Whether you're a student starting out, a finance professional planning a career pivot, or a startup founder facing a specific business challenge, Pay It Forward connects you with established industry professionals for face-to-face, one-to-one mentorship. It's a chance to get advice from people who have already worked through the challenges you're facing. Sessions are 15 minutes long and take place at the Pay It Forward Lounge in Hall 3, from 18 to 20 November, 1.10pm to 5.10pm. Come with one specific question or challenge, and leave with focused, practical advice.

title: Welcome to Ignite Stage - Day 3
description: Join us as we kick off the day's sessions on the Ignite Stage, featuring insightful conversations, groundbreaking ideas, and inspiring voices shaping the future of FinTech.

title: India Has Built the Rails. Will Global Capital Follow?
speakers: Siddharth Shetty; Keki Mistry; Vijay Shekhar Sharma; Rama Mohan Rao Amara; Nikunj Dalmia
description:
India has built the world's most widely used real-time payments system, a deep base of domestic investors and a fintech ecosystem that is setting global benchmarks. But can it translate this domestic scale into global financial leadership? Bringing together leaders from banking, fintech and digital public infrastructure, this session examines whether India's pioneering digital infrastructure can become the rails for global finance, what it will take to attract long-term international capital and how India can establish itself as a global financial hub.

Central Question: What will it take for global capital to see India not simply as a growth market, but as a home base for global finance?

title: Are Secondaries and Strategic Consolidations the Most Workable Exit Path Now?
speakers: Hero Choudhary; Dr. Kuo-Yi Lim; Joyce Ng; Dr. Rahul Banerjee
description: Venture survival depends on cash distributions, yet public listing routes remain narrow for Southeast Asian tech firms. Bain & Company's SEA Venture Capital Report highlights that while public IPO pipelines remain stalled across domestic bourses, secondary transactions, corporate consolidations, and private equity buyouts generated over $6 billion in regional exit value. With institutional LPs demanding realized DPI over unrealized paper gains, fund managers are redesigning liquidity timelines. This session analyses how leading allocators and founders are engineering secondary sales, structured earn-outs, and strategic trade sales when public capital markets stay constrained.
description_zh: 創投能否存續取決於現金分配，但東南亞科技公司的公開上市途徑仍然狹窄。貝恩公司（Bain & Company）的東南亞創投報告指出，儘管各國交易所的 IPO 進程仍陷於停滯，次級交易、企業整併及私募股權收購，已為該區域創造超過 60 億美元的退出價值。隨著機構有限合夥人（LP）要求已實現的投入資本分配倍數（DPI），而非尚未實現的帳面收益，基金經理人正重新設計流動性時程。本場次分析在公開資本市場持續受限時，領先的資本配置者與創辦人，如何安排次級股權出售、結構化績效對價及策略性出售。

title: The AI Dividend: Powering Resilient Service in Financial Institutions - Powered by Atlassian
description: As APAC financial institutions scale AI, leading firms are moving beyond siloed tools to capture a true AI Dividend. Grounded in new Atlassian & Mandala research, learn how frontier institutions are unifying business teams and using AI capacity gains to accelerate incident response, automate audit-readiness, and achieve operational resilience.

title: STUBBORN – Book Launch & Signing with Navin Suri
description: First 50 copies gets their book autographed by the author Navin Suri

title: Keeping Money Moving: Financial Resilience in an Age of Emerging Risks
speakers: Colin Payne; André Brunner; Thomas Moser; Hon. Jonathan Burke; Jael Tan
description:
As financial systems become more digital and interconnected, new technologies are reshaping the risks to their resilience. Quantum computing could eventually undermine the cryptography securing today’s financial infrastructure, frontier AI is changing the scale and sophistication of cyber threats and fraud, and the growth of tokenised money raises new questions about the reliability of the infrastructure on which it depends.

This session brings together perspectives from central banking, financial regulation and digital money to examine how the financial system can prepare for these risks before they materialise. What needs to happen now to ensure that emerging technologies strengthen financial infrastructure rather than create new points of failure?

title: The Napkin Pitch Is Dead. What Gets an Emerging-Market Fintech Funded?
speakers: Hon. Sunil Sabharwal; Mohammed Al-Emadi; Saemin Ahn; MP Oliveira; Nishtha Asthana
description: Capital hasn't left emerging-market fintech. It has just stopped funding the napkin. In the first half of 2026, Southeast Asian fintechs raised US$682 million and MENA fintechs raised US$617 million. In both regions a single round took a third or more of the total, and the number of deals fell sharply. Investors now want real revenue and a short road to profitability before they commit. Investors from the Gulf and North Asia sit alongside two Southeast Asian fintechs to compare what each market rewards, which metrics get a term sheet signed and what founders should ask of the investors they bring onto their cap table.
description_zh: 資本並未離開新興市場金融科技，只是不再為餐巾紙上的構想買單。2026 年上半年，東南亞金融科技公司募得 6.82 億美元，中東及北非（MENA）金融科技公司則募得 6.17 億美元。兩個區域都由單一融資輪占去總額的三分之一或更多，交易筆數也大幅下降。投資人如今要求先看到真實營收及短期內可實現獲利的路徑，才願意投入。來自海灣地區與北亞的投資人，將與兩家東南亞金融科技公司同台，比較各市場看重什麼、哪些指標能促成投資條款書簽署，以及創辦人在引入股東名冊上的投資人時，應向他們提出哪些要求。

title: The Next Profit Growth Point in International Payments - Powered by NovaPay
description: Traditional profit models in international payments are under pressure from falling fees, faster rails and new competitors. This session looks at where the next sources of growth lie across the payments value chain, from data services and embedded finance to cross-border treasury management and new forms of digital money. It examines how AI is reshaping the value chain, creating customer value and enabling new business models. Drawing on industry trends and real-world cases, it maps out the profit opportunities and commercialisation paths for payment institutions from 2027 onwards.

title: [Booth 2C25] Smarter Banking with Data, AI and Automation
description:
・Combining governed data, agentic AI, and intelligent managed services for financial institutions

・Enabling faster decisions, greater operational efficiency, and stronger mission-critical operations

・From modern data foundations and Customer 360 to AI-powered automation — trusted insights and always-on banking at enterprise scale

title: Asia’s Interoperable Green Economy: The Leap from National to Regional
speakers: Abigail Ng; Atty. Rogelio V. Quevedo; Christine Engstrom; Lionel Wong
description:
Sustainability data is no longer just a reporting requirement. As the impacts of climate change become more pronounced, trusted data on ESG performance will increasingly shape who companies buy from, who banks finance, and where capital flows.

But sustainability data remains difficult to generate, difficult to exchange, and difficult to translate into the commercial decisions it ought to inform. SMEs, which make up the overwhelming majority of businesses across Asia, often lack the motivation, time, resources and financial capacity to get started. Those that do face fragmented requirements, limited guidance and repeated requests for similar information from different customers, financiers and regulators.

Across Asia, governments and development institutions are rising to the challenge.

- In Singapore, the public and private sectors are collaborating on common digital infrastructure in the form of Green 100, that underpins nationwide activation of “queen bees” and their supply chains.

- The Philippines is similarly exploring how publicly listed companies can mobilise suppliers for Scope 3 reporting, ahead of their mandatory ISSB reporting timelines;

- India is examining how inclusive and simplified disclosures can enhance MSMEs’ access to green marketplaces globally and strengthen access to green trade financing from banks.

A common ambition cuts across these efforts – the shared desire to move from reporting towards reusable economic infrastructure, in which trusted sustainability data is generated once, but put to work repeatedly across compliance, supply chain, procurement, and financing use cases.

This dialogue brings together the SEC Philippines, ADB, RXIL and MAS to explore the steps needed to make this transition real. Who builds the rails? What gets businesses onto them? Where does public infrastructure end and private innovation begin? And can these emerging national approaches ‘interoperate’ to collectively power Asia’s transition toward a low carbon economy?

title: Welcome to Frontier Stage - Day 3
description: Join us as we kick off the day's sessions on the Frontier Stage, featuring insightful conversations, groundbreaking ideas, and inspiring voices shaping the future of FinTech.

title: Merchant Insights - Every Basis Point Matters: Finding the Hidden Margin in Global Payments
description:
Merchants spend months negotiating fractions of a cent with payment providers, yet far greater costs can remain hidden across routing, acceptance rates, cross-border fees, foreign exchange and failed transactions.

In this 30-minute fireside chat, go behind the scenes of global payment operations to understand where margin is lost, why standard pricing models may not reflect a merchant’s actual payment flows, and how leading digital platforms assess the true cost of every transaction.

Discover the data, operating decisions and optimisation strategies that can turn payments from a fixed expense into a source of measurable commercial value.

title: Payments Beyond Borders: Can Trust Transcend Geopolitical Boundaries? - Powered by NPCI
speakers: Anubhav Sharma; Amit Tendulkar; Bhavna Monga
description: As geopolitics redraws trade, capital and data flows, trusted payment infrastructure is becoming a strategic priority for nations. Drawing on experiences from India and ASEAN, the session will explore how countries can build resilient, inclusive and locally governed payment foundations while staying globally connected and examine practical approaches for linking domestic payment systems across bilateral and regional payment corridors.
description_zh: 隨著地緣政治重新描繪貿易、資本及資料的流向，可信的支付基礎設施正成為各國的策略優先事項。本場次將借鏡印度及東協的經驗，探討各國如何在維持全球連結的同時，建立具韌性、包容性且由本地治理的支付基礎，並檢視透過雙邊及區域支付走廊連結國內支付系統的實務做法。

title: Spark to Scale: How NUS Grows the Next Generation of Talent
speakers: Prof. Chia Tek Yew; Prof. Chai Kah Hin
description: Every leader started somewhere. At NUS, that start can come as early as age 15. Prof Chai Kah Hin of NUS SCALE and Prof Chia Tek Yew of NUS AIDF sit down together to show how a student’s first spark of interest can grow into a career in digital finance. The NUS Youth Programmes are where that spark begins. The Asian Institute of Digital Finance (AIDF) is where it turns into deep expertise and real-world impact. Find out how the two programmes connect, and why education can’t wait, especially as AI changes how money works.

title: Greg's Untold Founder Story
description: Incredible Hand-Picked Founder Stories Packed With Untold Insights and Inspiration. Exceptional start-up founders take the "yellow circle" to open up about their personal struggles and challenges, so that these stories may be a source of learning, encouragement, and inspiration for other entrepreneurs.

title: Beyond the Red Flag: When AI Sees What Humans Can’t​ - Powered by Accenture
description: Financial crime doesn't operate in silos, yet most fraud detection tools do. Today's landscape is filled with point solutions: KYC platforms that stop at onboarding, AML engines focused on transaction monitoring, and network graph tools that excel technically. Fraud signals are everywhere, but data remains fragmented. AI Fraud Surveillance unifies financial, qualitative, and network signals into a single view, enabling fraud detection before it happens, not after.
description_zh: 金融犯罪不會各自孤立地運作，但多數詐欺偵測工具卻是如此。今日市場充斥著單點解決方案：僅處理客戶開戶的 KYC 平台、聚焦交易監控的洗錢防制引擎，以及技術表現出色的網路關係圖工具。詐欺訊號無所不在，資料卻仍然零散。AI Fraud Surveillance 將財務、質性及網路訊號整合成單一視圖，讓詐欺得以在發生之前被偵測，而不是事後才發現。

title: The South–South Playbook: Rewiring Finance for the Remaining 1.6 Billion Unbanked
speakers: Dr. Patrick Njoroge; Parul Seth Khanna; Nasim Aliev; H.E. Hélder Lopes; Irene Arias Hofman
description: Emerging markets have built some of the world’s most innovative models for financial inclusion. This panel explores what Africa and Asia can learn directly from each other — from digital public infrastructure and payments to regulation and public-private partnerships — and whether a new South–South playbook can accelerate the next phase of financial inclusion.
description_zh: 新興市場已建立一些全球最具創新性的普惠金融模式。本場論壇探討非洲與亞洲可以直接向彼此學習什麼，範圍涵蓋數位公共基礎設施、支付、監管及公私協力合作，以及一套新的南南合作行動方針，能否加速普惠金融的下一階段發展。

title: The Road Not Taken
description: Incredible Hand-Picked Founder Stories Packed With Untold Insights and Inspiration. Exceptional start-up founders take the "yellow circle" to open up about their personal struggles and challenges, so that these stories may be a source of learning, encouragement, and inspiration for other entrepreneurs.

title: Catching Evolving Credit Risk Before Your Models Fall Behind - Powered by PFCT
description: Delinquency patterns shift faster than models can be retrained, and labeled examples of emerging risks are scarce. This session shows how a Tabular Foundation Model purpose-built for lending detected approximately 33% more early-delinquency cases than a quarterly-retrained ML model, without retraining. The speakers will explain how the model, relevant historical examples and an AI agent work together to support lending decisions, share lessons from development, and demonstrate the practical workflow.

title: Making Stablecoin Payments Work for Business - Powered by Circle
description: Stablecoins can move money across borders in minutes, but businesses still need payments to land locally, reconcile cleanly and stay compliant. A payments provider and a stablecoin issuer share what they learned from connecting through a stablecoin payment network: how network access, local payout and operational controls fit together, and what it really takes to integrate, onboard clients and run it every day.

title: ALFIN Demo Session
description: Discover first-hand the capabilities of ALFIN, presented by our ALFIN team.

title: [Booth 5F25] From data to decision: Building trusted agentic AI for insurance
description: Fireside chat "From data to decision: Building trusted agentic AI for insurance" - Speakers: Marc Hengen, CEO, Luxembourg Insurance and Reinsurance Association (ACA) and Fausto Pupo, Head of Delivery, Altilia

title: [Booth 2C25] From Vision to Reality: Building Collaborative AML in Japan
description:
・As financial crime crosses institutions and borders, AML/CFT operations face growing pressure from resource shortages, investigation workloads, fragmented information and cost

・finoject and Hitachi share their journey toward industry-wide collaborative AML in digital assets — from concept and PoC to commercial implementation — and examine what makes collaboration work in practice, from information sharing and governance to cost allocation and sustainability

title: [Booth 2E13] NP: Leveraging Behavioural Insights to Drive AI Transformation in UOB
description: Explore how organisations can move from shallow AI use to deeper, valuable and responsible adoption. Discover how motivation, capability and trust shape behaviour, and how simple nudges helped UOB increase average monthly Copilot training attendance ninefold and reach its training targets two months early.

title: The Future of Trust: Deepfakes, Synthetic Identity and Proof in the Age of Generative AI
speakers: Minh Nguyen; Iain Armstrong; Yair Tal; Aishwarya Jayakumar; Josef Jelinek
description:
In a world of synthetic everything, proof is becoming the scarcest commodity in finance. As AI-generated identities, deepfakes, and convincing digital deception become routine, institutions can no longer assume authenticity; they have to verify it. This session frames the problem and then works through the answer.

It opens with the shift underneath the shift: once trust can no longer be assumed, the burden moves from catching fakes after the fact to proving authenticity before a transaction happens at all. That reframes what needs to be provable rather than assumed, and who is positioned to build the systems that prove it. The discussion then gets specific about the different bets being placed on how to solve this: catching synthetic fraud at the point of verification, proving identity cryptographically without exposing the underlying data at all, and building the credential infrastructure that ties it together.

Attendees hear where each approach actually holds up against a motivated forger, and where the gaps between them still leave room for one to slip through.
description_zh: 在萬物皆可合成的世界中，證明正成為金融領域最稀缺的資源。隨著 AI 生成身分、深偽技術及足以亂真的數位欺騙變得常見，機構已無法假定事物真實，而必須加以驗證。本場次先界定問題，再逐步探索答案。首先探討變革背後更深一層的轉變：一旦信任不再能被視為理所當然，責任重點便從事後抓出偽造，轉向在交易發生之前就證明真實性。這重新界定了哪些事項必須能被證明、而不能只是預設成立，以及誰有條件建造提供這些證明的系統。接著，討論將具體檢視不同的解題途徑：在驗證環節攔截合成詐欺、在完全不暴露底層資料的情況下以密碼學證明身分，以及建構將各環節串接起來的憑證基礎設施。與會者將聽到各種方法在哪些情況下確實能抵擋蓄意偽造者，以及方法之間的哪些缺口仍可能讓偽造者趁隙而入。

title: Alfin: Your FinTech Knowledge Agent
description: ALFIN by GFTN brings you what's said on the stages of GFTN's forums, live, and answers your questions on finance and technology, with sources.

title: Launch of the RE:Build Challenge – Reimagining Asia’s Built Sector for a Super Low Energy Future
description:
What would it take to transform today’s built infrastructure into tomorrow’s Super Low Energy buildings? RE:Build brings together building owners, technology providers, industry partners and project financiers to answer this question.

Powered by BCA’s Super Low Energy Building Smart Hub (SLEB-SH), developed by Hitachi, RE:Build will see developers and building owners volunteer existing projects for innovative solution providers to model how their technologies could improve energy performance and bridge the gap between buildings’ current and potential future Green Mark performance.

Getting the technology right is only half the equation. RE:Build will simultaneously explore the business case for retrofits – examining how improvements in energy and emissions performance translate into measurable economic value through operating savings, financing benefits, enhanced asset value, incentives, and emerging avenues for monetising green performance.

First announced at the 2026 Singapore FinTech Festival, RE:Build will launch in 1H 2027 as a common innovation sandbox with the ambition of developing replicable models for accelerating green building retrofits across Asia; and in doing so, demonstrating how the economics of going green can work for the owners investing in them.

title: Stablecoins and the Future of Corporate Treasury - Powered by Mobi Asia
description: What if corporate treasury didn't need banks, borders, or business hours to move money? This session imagines a future where corporates hold, move, and grow liquidity globally on their own terms, and what it would take to get there.

title: Making Business Payments Agentic with Google Cloud
Can An AI Wrapper Ever Become a Scalable Business?
speakers: Abhishek Chatterjee; Richard Tong; Rosaline Chow Koo; Shameek Kundu
description: Adding conversational wrappers and light automation layers over third-party models provided quick early ARR, but enterprise buyers are cutting through the veneer. Carta’s State of Private Markets analysis reveals that software companies driven by signed enterprise workflow contracts trade at a median 11.8x revenue, whereas startups reliant on pilot or usage-based AI features clear at just 5.2x. Furthermore, McKinsey’s enterprise AI research highlights that fewer than 20% of adopting companies report bottom-line EBIT impact. This session equips founders to construct defensible domain data integrations and proprietary workflows that survive upstream platform commoditization.
description_zh: 在第三方模型上加上對話式介面及輕量自動化層，曾快速帶來早期年度經常性收入（ARR），但企業買方正逐漸看穿這層包裝。Carta 的《私募市場現況》分析顯示，以已簽署的企業工作流程合約驅動業務的軟體公司，其交易估值營收倍數中位數為 11.8 倍；依賴試點或按使用量計費 AI 功能的新創公司，則僅為 5.2 倍。此外，麥肯錫的企業 AI 研究指出，採用 AI 的公司中，不到 20% 回報息稅前利潤（EBIT）受到實質影響。本場次將協助創辦人建立具有競爭防禦力的領域資料整合與專有工作流程，使企業能在上游平台同質化的過程中存續。

title: C:\>DIR Agentic Regulator Showcase
speakers: Probe (Multiply AI); Agent Reliability Profile (ML Commons); Team Axiom (State Bank of Pakistan); Rwanda Anti Scams Team (National Bank of Rwanda, Proto and FNA); YU-SAM POWER (University College London); Team Phoenix (Securities and Exchange Board of India); Maha El Dimachki; Bryan Zhang
description:
AI agents are already executing workflows and making decisions at machine speed across financial systems and digital markets. Supervisors are being asked to oversee them with tools built for a slower world.

The Cambridge Digital Innovation and Regulation Initiative (C:\>DIR), hosted by Financial Innovation for Impact launched the Global 'Agentic Regulator' Hackathon in September this year.

The hackathon brought together multidisciplinary teams from the public and private sectors to work on that gap, building explainable, deployable prototypes across six priority areas:

- Agentic Financial and High Stakes AI Advice (supported by Moneybox)

- Agentic Payments, Commerce & their Oversight (supported by Ant International)

- Decentralised Market Infrastructure, Smart Contracts & AI Agents (supported by the Ethereum Foundation)

- AI-Driven Fraud and Scams

- Know Your Agent (KY-A), Digital Verification and Digital Public Infrastructure

- Market Manipulation, Agentic Herding & Stability

The winning teams now bring their work to the Catalyst Stage at the Singapore FinTech Festival. Come and see what the future of supervision could look like.
description_zh: AI 代理已在金融系統及數位市場中，以機器速度執行工作流程並做出決策。監理者卻被要求使用為較慢節奏世界打造的工具來監督它們。由 Financial Innovation for Impact 承辦的 Cambridge Digital Innovation and Regulation Initiative（C:\>DIR），於今年 9 月推出全球「Agentic Regulator」黑客松。活動匯聚公私部門的跨領域團隊，針對這項落差，在六個優先領域建構可解釋、可部署的原型：代理型金融與高風險 AI 諮詢（由 Moneybox 支持）；代理型支付、商業及其監督（由 Ant International 支持）；去中心化市場基礎設施、智慧合約與 AI 代理（由 Ethereum Foundation 支持）；AI 驅動的詐欺與詐騙；認識你的代理（KY-A）、數位驗證及數位公共基礎設施；市場操縱、代理群聚行為與穩定性。獲勝團隊現在將把成果帶到新加坡金融科技節的 Catalyst Stage。一起來看看監理的未來可能是什麼樣貌。

title: Investor Hours: Startup-Investor Matchmaking
description:
Over 500 startups and 200 investors from 50+ markets meet at Investor Hours annually for fundraising, deal sharing, investment and market expansion opportunities.

We invite startups across sectors and stages to request investor meetings, and investors to meet startups for deal opportunities and fellow investors for deal sharing.

Meetings are pre-scheduled within Investor Hours in SFF App and curated by GFTN team in 15min slots.

Registration is required: https://www.fintechfestival.sg/investor-hours

title: Money Without Borders? Rewiring Payments for Emerging Markets
speakers: Ola Oyetayo; Pratyush Prasanna; Ramana Kumar; Tian Tian Chua
description:
Digital payments can move at the tap of a screen; cross-border money still has to navigate fragmented rails, uneven access to foreign exchange, regulatory complexity and the realities of local markets. As trade and digital commerce deepen across Africa and Asia, what will it take to make international payments faster, more transparent and more inclusive?

This conversation will bring operator and market perspectives to a central question: can the next generation of payment systems serve emerging-market businesses on their own terms? The discussion will explore where innovation is making a difference, what still holds corridors back, and how providers can build trust and scale across borders.

title: Envision the Last Mile: Tomorrow’s Payments, Today - Powered by dtcpay
description: The Three Shifts of AI Payments Decide. AI assistants are becoming the gateway to commerce, and until they solve what to buy, how to pay is a castle in the air. Pay. An agent can start a payment, but only a merchant can accept it, and stablecoins are the closest thing to an open layer across today's closed issuing and acquiring systems. Trust. Agent payments and human-in-the-loop pull in opposite directions; only trust, built on AI-powered compliance and licensed data custody, lets humans move from approving every payment to setting the rules.

title: Anchoring Digital Financial Markets
speakers: Aaron Seabrook; Rahul Advani; Dr. Wolfram Seidemann; Isadora Arredondo; Chengyi Ong
description:
Tokenisation has moved well past the pilot stage, but a market only works if the infrastructure underneath it can be trusted: networks built for institutional scale, platforms that connect issuance, trading and settlement, a trusted form of money to settle in, and an infrastructure that lets institutions run digital assets as everyday business. This panel brings together the people building each of those layers.

The discussion works through what each layer needs to hold up under real institutional volumes, where the handoffs between networks, platforms, settlement money and legacy systems still cause friction, and what the operating model behind digital assets looks like in practice: who runs what, how it connects to existing infrastructure, and what it takes to scale. Attendees leave with a practical view of what "anchoring" digital markets means, from the network to the money that settles on it.
description_zh: 代幣化早已跨越試點階段，但市場要能運作，底層基礎設施就必須值得信賴：為機構規模打造的網路、連結發行、交易及結算的平台、可信賴的結算貨幣，以及讓機構能將數位資產作為日常業務運作的基礎設施。本場論壇匯聚建構各個層次的實務工作者。討論將逐一探討每個層次需要什麼才能承受真實的機構交易量、網路、平台、結算貨幣及傳統系統之間的銜接在哪裡仍造成阻力，以及數位資產背後的營運模式實際是什麼樣貌：誰負責什麼、如何連接既有基礎設施，以及擴大規模需要哪些條件。與會者將從網路到其上用於結算的貨幣，務實了解為數位市場「奠定穩固基礎」的含義。

title: From Invisible to Investable: Building the Financial Infrastructure for the Next Billion
speakers: Richard Budel; Allen Forlemu; Munir Duri; Jean-Marie Kananura; Francesca Aliverti
description: Billions of people and small businesses remain outside formal credit because financial institutions cannot reliably identify, assess or price their risk. This panel examines how payment infrastructure, digital identity, transaction data and AI can change that — turning previously invisible economic activity into a basis for lending and investment.
description_zh: 數十億人口及小型企業仍無法取得正規信貸，因為金融機構無法可靠地辨識、評估其風險或為風險定價。本場論壇探討支付基礎設施、數位身分、交易資料及 AI 如何改變這種情況，將過去不可見的經濟活動轉化為放款與投資的依據。

title: Quantum-Powered Financial Fraud Detection with CVQBoost - Powered by Quantum Computing
description: Live demonstration of CVQBoost, a quantum-powered machine learning algorithm for financial fraud detection using Dirac-3. We demonstrate fast model training, competitive accuracy, and scalability to millions of transactions compared with classical XGBoost.

title: From Data Chaos to AI-Ready: The Agent Behind Every Insurance Advisor - Powered by Microsoft
description: AI's real blocker isn't the model, it's unstructured data. This live demo shows an agent that scans external market signals, matches them to an advisor's book, and turns a headline into a qualified proposal, so advisors arrive don't just walk in prepared, they proactively create the next opportunity. See Microsoft's Work IQ, Foundry IQ, Fabric IQ and Web IQ orchestrating as one platform to make this a reality.
description_zh: AI 真正的阻礙不是模型，而是非結構化資料。本次現場示範將展示一個代理，掃描外部市場訊號、與顧問的客戶組合配對，並將一則新聞標題轉化為經篩選的合適提案，讓顧問不只是有備而來，更能主動創造下一個機會。看看 Microsoft 的 Work IQ、Foundry IQ、Fabric IQ 及 Web IQ 如何整合協作成單一平台，讓這一切成真。

Drawing on cases from Southeast Asia and Latin America, this session explores AI execution and AI-assisted oversight across feature engineering, modelling and credit strategy. Attendees will see a practical workflow, its evaluation results, and where human judgement remains essential.
description_zh: AI 正如何改變信貸決策背後的工作？本場次借鏡東南亞及拉丁美洲的案例，探討特徵工程、建模及信貸策略中的 AI 執行與 AI 輔助監督。與會者將看到實際工作流程、評估結果，以及哪些環節仍不可或缺地需要人類判斷。

title: Can Europe and Asia Build the Next Global Wealth Corridor?
speakers: Lavanya Chari; Alex Panican; Prof. R. Alexander Lorz; Nishtha Asthana
description: Europe and Asia have capital, investment products and increasingly global investors, but the infrastructure connecting them remains fragmented. Different regulations, fund structures, data standards and distribution systems continue to limit access and raise costs. This session examines what it would take to create a trusted wealth corridor between the regions, from regulatory interoperability and digital fund distribution to common data and identity rails. It asks how governments, financial centres, asset managers, banks and fintech platforms can reduce friction without weakening investor protection.
description_zh: 歐洲與亞洲擁有資本、投資產品，以及日益全球化的投資人，但連結兩地的基礎設施仍然零散。不同的法規、基金結構、資料標準及分銷系統，持續限制市場接入並推高成本。本場次探討建立兩地之間可信財富走廊所需的條件，範圍從監管互通、數位基金分銷，到共通資料及身分基礎通道。討論將檢視政府、金融中心、資產管理業者、銀行及金融科技平台，如何在不削弱投資人保護的前提下減少阻力。

title: Scaling Tokenization: New Efficiencies, New Vulnerabilities
speakers: Kleopatra Nikolaou; Manisha Patel; Mindaugas Leika; Khyati Chauhan
description: Tokenization has moved beyond pilots into repo, money market funds and bond issuance, yet activity remains small and spread across siloed, permissioned platforms. Atomic settlement, programmable collateral and round-the-clock trading are stripping cost and reconciliation from the asset life cycle. The same features also remove the timing gaps and intermediaries that traditionally absorb liquidity and operational shocks. When settlement leaves no time to react, where does resilience come from? This session examines which gains depend on a shared ledger, what legal certainty and safe settlement must deliver before markets scale, and how safeguards work when markets never close.

title: Programmable Money and the Rise of Agentic Payments
speakers: Jason Newin; Tin Pei Ling; Mai Kaneko; Kennie Ong
description:
Money is becoming programmable. Stablecoins, tokenized bank deposits and central bank digital currencies can now carry rules about when, where and to whom they move. Banks, card networks and fintechs are building on these new forms of money, and AI agents are starting to transact on their own. But the landscape is fragmented across issuers, networks and jurisdictions, and money that works in one system may not be accepted in another. As payments become conditional, automated and increasingly initiated by machines rather than people, the questions get sharper. How do we preserve the “singleness of money” when there are many monies? What frameworks allow businesses send value across borders as easily as a message? And when an agent pays, who carries the responsibility?

The panel will separate what is working today from what is still hype, and set out what the industry and businesses need to get right next.

title: Beyond Faster Payments: What’s Still Holding Cross-Border Payments Back?
speakers: Shadab Taiyabi; Ben Wong; Violas Xiao; Jeremy Tan; Pieter Franken
description:
For years, the payments industry has shared one ambition: make cross-border payments faster, cheaper, more transparent and more inclusive. Progress has been made, but the hardest problems are no longer technical. Firms moving money across borders still face differing compliance requirements, inconsistent standards, limited interoperability and persistent first- and last-mile frictions. These costs fall hardest on merchants and small businesses.

With the G20’s 2027 targets for cross-border payments approaching, the question is what can actually be delivered, and by whom.

This session brings together practitioners who move money across borders every day, from merchant acquiring and cross-border platforms to the fintech industry. It looks at Asia’s corridors, where markets operate at very different stages of development. Which bottlenecks cost businesses most? What has worked in practice? And where does industry need to act together, or need policymakers to step in, to turn ambition into measurable progress?

description: AI is changing software testing, but can financial institutions trust what it generates? Using a live demonstration of AI-assisted test generation, human review and automated execution, this session explores how to accelerate banking QA while managing errors, coverage gaps and accountability. Attendees will learn practical controls for adopting AI in critical financial systems.

title: Prototype Rich, Capital Poor: Fixing the University-to-Market Gap
speakers: Prof. Sameer Hasija; Bryan Zhang; Prof. Shonali Krishnaswamy; Sharanjit Leyl
description:
Universities are some of the most productive IP engines in the world. Researchers and students build new technology, file patents and often ship working prototypes. Then too much of it stalls. The people who invent are rarely the people who raise money, price a licence or find a first customer. Tech transfer offices work to academic timelines while capital works to market ones, so good IP sits on the shelf.

This panel asks two questions. First, what should universities change so their IP becomes investable: spin-out terms, founder support, equity and licensing models, and incentives for faculty? Second, should investors stop waiting for deals to show up and go into campuses to find them? We'll look at what each side gets wrong about the other, and what a working lab-to-market pipeline looks like.

title: Skills Gaps and the Shape of Tomorrow's Financial Institutions
speakers: Yang Dongye; Mostapha Tahiri; Jayaram Iyer; Osamu Abe; Akanksha Rath
description: Talent rewiring is redrawing the map itself, institutions now follow people first, capital and headquarters second. Financial institutions increasingly decide where to build based on where the talent already is, not just where capital or headquarters sit. This discussion looks at how that dynamic is redrawing where financial institutions locate technology and operations, and what it means for markets competing to become talent hubs rather than just financial centres. The key question it looks to answer: is the future of finance shaped more by where the talent is than by where the capital is?

title: [Booth 5D25] Behavioral Intelligence in Action: Live Scoring Demo
description:
Ever wondered what device footprints reveal about risky behaviours? Join Credolab for a live, interactive demonstration of behavioural intelligence at work. See how non-intrusive metadata transforms into real-time risk scores that help risk teams approve more applicants safely.

What you’ll see:

- Live data capture to score: Step-by-step walkthrough of how behavioural signals are captured, anonymised, and converted into predictive risk scores in seconds.

- Behavioural scorecard walkthrough: Experience the behavioural risk scorecard, including granular behavioural predictors.

- Fraud vs. Credit risk signals: How subtle interaction patterns flag synthetic identity, device manipulation, and intent to default.

title: The Missing Middle: Powering the Next Wave of Commercial Payment Corridors
speakers: Anouska Ladds; Anupam Pahuja; Clara Shi; Nischita Hejmady; Kaitlyn Thinn
description: While most payments conversations focus on consumer rails, the real bottleneck may be commercial: B2B and merchant payments across Asia, the Middle East and Africa remain fragmented and cash-heavy. This panel unpacks what it takes to build commercial payment corridors that actually work and where the friction still lies.
description_zh: 多數支付討論聚焦消費者支付通道，但真正的瓶頸可能在商業支付：亞洲、中東及非洲的企業對企業（B2B）與商家支付仍然零散，並高度依賴現金。本場論壇解析打造真正有效的商業支付走廊需要具備什麼，以及阻力仍存在於哪些環節。

title: The Super App Next Door: How Consumer Ecosystems Take Root
speakers: Vince Iswara; Khodjaev Amirkhon; Josef Jelinek
description:
From Central Asia to Southeast Asia, digital platforms are bringing payments, commerce and everyday services together in a single consumer experience. But there is no universal blueprint for a super app: each ecosystem grows from local habits, trusted services and the infrastructure people already use.

This conversation will examine what makes consumer ecosystems relevant and resilient. How do platforms earn a place in daily life? Which services create a path from first use to lasting engagement? And as ecosystems expand, how can they balance convenience, competition and consumer trust?

title: Asia's Payments Moment: Building Connectivity Across ASEAN and Beyond
speakers: Atty. Bridget Rose Mesina-Romero; Sakkapop Panyanukul; Benjamin Lee
description:
Bilateral links between Asia's national instant-payment systems already exist and are multiplying. QR code interoperability between several member states has been live for years, built one country pair at a time. The next opportunity is a genuinely connected system, one where a payment initiated in any linked market settles instantly in any other, without each pair of countries negotiating its own bridge. Emerging multilateral models such as Nexus show how the region and beyond could move beyond corridor-by-corridor integration. As Singapore prepares to take over the ASEAN chairmanship from the Philippines in 2027, regional payment connectivity is shaping up to be one of the flagship items on its agenda, and this session is where that opportunity gets mapped out, a year ahead of time.

This panel brings together central bank representatives from across ASEAN and India to discuss what a genuinely connected instant-payment system could unlock: aligning local-currency settlement frameworks, building on the links already in place, from ASEAN's QR interoperability to the UPI-PayNow corridor, to reach true multilateral interoperability, and establishing the shared governance that lets partners trust a system built together rather than one at a time. Attendees leave with a clear view of the progress already made, what Singapore's incoming ASEAN chairmanship could prioritise, and how close the wider region actually is to instant payments that work the same way whether you're paying across the street or across a border.

title: Criminals Deployed Agents First. Can Real-Time Controls Catch Up?
speakers: Vincent Li; Venus Leung; Jackson Hull; Jan Morgenthal; Pieter Franken
description: Fraudsters didn't wait for a governance framework. Autonomous agents are already probing payment rails, spinning up synthetic identities and running social-engineering scripts at machine speed, while many institutions still triage alerts in batches. With instant payments and agentic commerce scaling fast, the window between attack and response is now measured in milliseconds. The panel looks at where real-time controls are keeping pace and where they are structurally behind. It also covers how to tell a legitimate customer's agent from a malicious one, and what defending with agents looks like when regulators still expect a human in the loop.
description_zh: 詐欺者並沒有等待治理架構到位。自主代理早已開始探測支付通道、建立合成身分，並以機器速度執行社交工程腳本，許多機構卻仍然以批次方式分流處理警報。隨著即時支付及代理型商業快速擴張，從攻擊到回應的時間窗口如今已以毫秒計算。本場論壇探討即時控管在哪些地方跟得上，又在哪些地方結構性落後。也將討論如何區分合法客戶的代理與惡意代理，以及當監管機關仍要求人類介入時，運用代理防禦會是什麼樣貌。

title: From Cash to Global Finance: Connecting the Rails of Digital Payments
speakers: Stanislav Skvirsky; Syed Mohammad Kamal; Alvin Okari; Anikó Szombati
description:
A QR code is only as useful as the network behind it. In markets where people still rely on cash, payment agents and kiosks can provide a crucial entry point to digital services. But turning that access into a dependable payment ecosystem also requires banks’ transaction systems to work smoothly and local networks to connect with the wider financial world.

This panel will examine the often-invisible connections that make digital payments work at scale. How do cash networks and digital rails reinforce each other? What needs to change inside financial institutions to make payments faster and more interoperable? And how can fintech ecosystems collaborate across borders without losing sight of local needs?

title: The Uneven Map: Where AI Rewrites Commerce First
speakers: Prasanna Varadharajan; Kunal Guha; Eun Mi Kristina Rhee; Tang Wei
description:
The protocol race is over faster than anyone expected. Visa, Google, Mastercard, OpenAI, Stripe and Ant International have all shipped agent-initiated payment infrastructure, while countries such as Korea alone recorded over 100 million AI-to-AI payments in seven months. This discussion will be around where machine will transact first, at what granularity, and on whose stack.

That question does not have a global answer, because agentic commerce is gated by four preconditions that are unevenly distributed or agreed upon.

Identity: can an agent be issued a provable, scoped, revocable mandate.

Acceptance density: is there enough merchant coverage for an agent's choice to be meaningful.

Settlement granularity: can value move at machine speed and sub-cent size.

Customer trust and value: will people actually delegate? Does the result make everyday finance simpler, more transparent and more accessible, including for customers that conventional banking has overlooked?

The first three are being solved on the rails; the fourth is decided in the customer relationship. This panel puts both views on one stage: the platforms building agentic infrastructure, and a digital bank that rebuilt banking around customer needs. Together they map the next eighteen months by looking look at where AI creates practical customer value first and how institutions should balance automation with human judgment and accountability.
description_zh: 協定競賽結束得比任何人預期都快。Visa、Google、Mastercard、OpenAI、Stripe 及 Ant International 都已推出由代理發起的支付基礎設施；在部分國家中，光是韓國就在七個月內記錄了逾 1 億筆 AI 對 AI 支付。本場討論將圍繞機器會先在哪裡交易、以多細的粒度交易，以及使用誰的技術架構展開。這個問題沒有全球通用的答案，因為代理型商業受四項前提限制，而它們的分布或共識並不均衡。身分：能否向代理核發可驗證、範圍明確且可撤銷的授權。受理密度：商家覆蓋是否足夠，讓代理的選擇具有意義。結算粒度：價值能否以機器速度、低於一分的金額移轉。客戶信任與價值：人們真的會委託代理嗎？結果是否讓日常金融變得更簡單、透明且容易取得，包括對傳統銀行業忽略的客戶而言？前三項正透過底層通道解決，第四項則取決於客戶關係。本場論壇將兩種觀點帶到同一舞台：建構代理型基礎設施的平台，以及一家圍繞客戶需求重新打造銀行服務的數位銀行。他們將共同勾勒未來十八個月的發展，探討 AI 會先在哪些地方為客戶創造實際價值，以及機構應如何平衡自動化、人類判斷與問責。

title: AI Scientist Entrepreneurs: From AI Research & Innovation to Entrepreneurship
speakers: Bahar Abbas Pour; Dr. Zhixi Cai; Abhijeet Narang; Prof. Joseph Liu; Prof. Shonali Krishnaswamy
description: History shows how breakthrough scientific discoveries can reshape the world. From Edgar F. Codd’s relational databases and Tim Berners-Lee’s World Wide Web to Mark Weiser’s vision of ubiquitous computing, pioneering technology research has transformed industries, economies and everyday life. Today, Artificial Intelligence presents a similarly transformative opportunity. A new generation of scientist-entrepreneurs in AI has the potential to translate frontier research into breakthrough technologies, products and ventures that redefine industries and address humanity’s greatest challenges. Their journey is not simply about commercialising discoveries, but about turning bold scientific ideas (developed through years of research) into innovations driving deep tech enterprises. The challenge is to create a sustainable pathway for academic innovations and scientist entrepreneurs to cross the bridge from science to enterprise seamlessly.
